# Independent Card — OB01: Paid Use of Plastic Shopping Bags

## Why this is an independent card

This is a real national regulation selected for **OB01 — A law or regulation about environmental protection**. It is separate from the Ershou Lake story because the lake cleanup has no verified legal title.

The central chain is:

> national regulation → effective from 1 June 2008 → supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets → plastic shopping bags must be sold rather than given away → clear price → encourage people to use fewer bags → conserve resources and protect the environment

---

## 1. Verified facts

- The official Chinese title is **《商品零售场所塑料购物袋有偿使用管理办法》**.
- It was issued jointly by the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission, and the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce.
- It took effect on **1 June 2008**.
- It applies to retail venues including supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets.
- These retailers must charge consumers for plastic shopping bags and clearly display the price.
- They may not provide the bags free of charge or disguise a free bag through another promotion.
- The stated purpose is to conserve resources, protect the environment, and encourage consumers to use fewer plastic shopping bags.
- A later national measure effective in 2023 still requires retail businesses to follow this paid-use regulation.

---

## 2. Speakable English blocks

### Introduce the regulation

> I'd like to talk about China's regulation on the paid use of plastic shopping bags.

### Explain the rule

> It took effect in 2008 and requires supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets to charge customers for plastic shopping bags instead of giving them away for free.

### Explain the purpose

> Its main purpose is to reduce unnecessary use of plastic bags, conserve resources, and protect the environment.

### Explain why the design makes sense

> The rule does not completely ban plastic bags. Instead, it makes their cost visible, which can encourage shoppers to bring reusable bags or think twice before taking a new one.

---

## 3. Useful vocabulary

- paid use of plastic shopping bags
- charge customers for a bag
- provide something free of charge
- display the price clearly
- retail venue
- supermarket / shopping mall / open market
- reusable shopping bag
- reduce unnecessary consumption
- conserve resources
- plastic pollution
- environmental regulation

---

## 4. One-minute preparation keywords

> China → 2008 → paid plastic bags → supermarkets / malls / markets → no free bags → clear price → fewer unnecessary bags → reusable bags → resources + environment

---

## 5. Factual boundaries

- Call it a **regulation** or **administrative measure**, not necessarily a law passed by the legislature.
- Do not say China completely banned all plastic bags.
- The paid-use rule concerns plastic shopping bags supplied by retail venues. It excludes certain plastic pre-packaging bags used for hygiene and food-safety purposes, such as bags for loose fresh or cooked food.
- Do not connect this national regulation to the cleanup of Ershou Lake.

---

## 6. Official sources

- [国家发展改革委：《商品零售场所塑料购物袋有偿使用管理办法》](https://www.ndrc.gov.cn/xxgk/zcfb/fzggwl/200805/t20080528_960713.html) — official text, effective 1 June 2008.
- [商务部：《商务领域经营者使用、报告一次性塑料制品管理办法》](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zfxxgk/zc/gz/art/2024/art_7669e841461a4d73805e16f345e88579.html) — Article 9 continues to require retail operators to follow the paid-use regulation; effective 20 June 2023.

# Core Story 005 — My Sister's Education Decisions

## Why this is a core story

This card contains two real decisions involving the same family member. Use the university-choice event for **giving advice** and the later postgraduate-study decision for **feeling proud of a family member**. Do not merge the two timelines into one event.

The EV17 chain is:

> sister finishes an important exam → grades limit the available choices → she also has preferences about majors → my mother and I research universities with her → compare universities and majors → narrow down the options → help her make a final choice → feel relieved

The separate EV18 chain is:

> sister has a stable job → decides to leave it → pursues the postgraduate degree she genuinely wants → accepts uncertainty instead of staying only for security → I admire her courage and feel proud of her

Do not memorize a full answer. Memorize the decision-making process.

---

## 1. Background

- This happened several years ago when my sister needed to choose a university.
- Her exam results were an important factor because they affected which universities she could realistically apply to.
- She also had her own preferences about what subject or major she wanted to study.
- My mother and I helped her research the available choices.

---

## 2. What we actually did

- We searched online for universities that matched her grades.
- We looked at the majors available at different universities.
- We compared several options instead of choosing the first one we found.
- We considered both practical limits and her own interests.
- We discussed the advantages and disadvantages together.
- Finally, we helped her narrow the list down and make a decision.

A natural sentence:

> My mother and I helped my sister research different universities and compare the majors they offered, based on both her grades and what she was interested in.

---

## 3. Why this was real collaboration

This was not only one person giving help.

- My sister had to explain what she wanted.
- My mother and I helped collect and compare information.
- We discussed the options together.
- The final choice was made through a shared decision-making process.

This makes the story useful for a **working-with-a-family-member** question if that question appears in another speaking bank.

Possible line:

> We worked on it together because each of us contributed something different: my sister knew what she wanted, while my mother and I helped her compare the realistic options.

---

## 4. Strong route — EV17: A time when you gave advice to others

### Best spotlight

Focus on:

> sister needs to choose university → many options → research → compare majors and universities → give advice → final decision

### What the advice was

The advice was not simply:

> “Choose this university.”

It was more like:

> choose an option that matches both your academic results and your genuine interest in the subject.

Possible line:

> I tried not to make the decision for her. Instead, I helped her compare the choices and encouraged her to think about both the university and the major.

## 5. Strong route — EV18: A time when you felt proud of a family member

This is a separate, later decision from the university-choice event above.

- My sister had a stable job.
- She chose to give it up so that she could pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted.
- The decision meant leaving security behind and accepting uncertainty.
- I felt proud of her because she had the courage to choose the path she truly valued.

Factual boundary:

- Do not claim that she completed the degree, entered a named programme, or achieved a particular result unless those facts are confirmed later.

## 6. Family-help route

# Core Story 006 — Renhe Xincheng: A Convenient but Boring Shopping Center

## Why this is a core story

This is a real place near my home that can naturally cover three topics:

- **PL05 — A boring place**
- **PL07 — A tall building in your city you like or dislike**
- **PL08 — A shopping mall**

The central idea is not that the shopping center has nothing in it. In fact, it has many normal facilities. The reason I find it boring is that **the experience feels repetitive and not very innovative**.

The central chain is:

> shopping center near my home → clothes / coffee / food / cinema / promotions → I sometimes go with friends or family → every visit feels similar → nothing feels unique → convenient but boring

---

## 1. Basic background

- The shopping center is called **Renhe Xincheng**.
- It is near my home.
- It is a tall commercial building.
- Its exterior looks like an ordinary high-rise and has not left a distinctive visual impression on me.
- It has common facilities such as:
  - clothing shops
  - coffee shops
  - restaurants or food options
  - a cinema
- It sometimes has promotional activities or small events.

---

## 2. What I usually do there

### With friends

- I mainly go there to watch movies.
- The cinema is probably the main reason I visit with friends.

### With family

- I sometimes go there with my parents.
- We may have coffee or spend a little time there.

A natural sentence:

> I don't go there because I love shopping. Most of the time, I only go there to watch a movie with friends or have a coffee with my parents.

---

## 3. Why I find it boring

The problem is **not** that there are no activities.

The real problem is:

- the shops are very similar to those in many other malls
- the promotions feel repetitive
- there is not much that feels new or surprising
- most of the activities are things I could do in almost any shopping center
- after a short time, I feel there is nothing else I really want to explore

A strong natural explanation:

> Even though there are quite a few things to do, I still find it boring because every visit feels almost the same. The shops, promotions, and activities are quite predictable, so there is rarely anything that makes me curious or excited.

---

## 4. What an interesting shopping center should be like

This is a useful extension if you need more ideas.

For me, an interesting shopping center should:

- have something distinctive
- offer activities that are hard to find elsewhere
- change its events or exhibitions regularly
- give people a reason to visit beyond basic shopping, coffee, or movies

A natural line:

> Personally, I think a good shopping center should have something unique that makes people want to go there specifically, rather than offering the same things you can find everywhere else.

---

## 5. Cue Card A — PL05: A boring place

### Best spotlight

Focus on:

> near my home → looks convenient → many ordinary facilities → I have visited many times → every visit feels repetitive → nothing unique → bored

### Useful structure

1. Where it is
2. Why you went there
3. What you can do there

### Possible reflection

> Looking back, I think the place is useful rather than enjoyable. I go there when I need something specific, but I rarely go there just for fun.

---

### Best spotlight

For the shopping-mall question, do not make the whole answer negative.

Focus on:

> location → facilities → who you go with → what you usually do → your balanced opinion

A balanced conclusion:

> It is convenient because it is close to my home and has most of the basic things I need, but I wouldn't call it exciting because there is not much that feels distinctive.

---

### Best spotlight

The dislike is about my personal emotional response, not a claim that the building is unsafe or badly designed.

They remind me of the fast pace and competitive pressure of a large city, whereas a small detached house feels more natural and has a stronger sense of everyday life.

# Core Story 007 — My Smartphone: Expensive but Essential

## Why this is a core story

This is one real object that supports two cue cards:

- **OB10 — An item on which you spent more than expected:** content-ready.
- **OB15 — Something you cannot live without:** content-ready.

The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes:

- **OB10:** focus on the purchase, budget, and why the final cost was higher than expected.
- **OB15:** focus on how often you use the phone and why it has become essential in daily life.

The central chain is:

> previous 256 GB experience required deleting apps → planned to buy another 256 GB smartphone → changed to the 512 GB version at the time of purchase → paid about 2,000 yuan more → no longer worry about storage → worth the extra cost → use it every day

---

## 1. Basic background

- The object is my smartphone.
- My previous 256 GB phone often ran short of storage, so I regularly deleted apps that I did not use very often.
- I originally planned to buy the 256 GB version.
- At the time of purchase, I suddenly decided to buy the 512 GB version instead.
- The storage upgrade made the final cost higher than I had expected.
- After upgrading, I no longer needed to worry about storage space, so I felt the extra cost was worthwhile.
- Even so, I use it every day and depend on it for many practical tasks.

---

## 2. Strong route — OB10: An item on which you spent more than expected

**Status: content-ready.**

### Best spotlight

Focus on:

> previous 256 GB storage problem → planned 256 GB version → changed my mind at purchase → chose 512 GB → paid about 2,000 yuan more → no storage anxiety → worthwhile

### Confirmed reason the cost was higher

> I originally planned to buy the 256 GB version, but I changed my mind at the time of purchase and chose the 512 GB version instead. That sudden storage upgrade made the phone cost more than I had expected.

- The approximate difference was **2,000 yuan**.
- With 512 GB, I no longer had to keep deleting less frequently used apps.
- I felt the extra cost was worthwhile because it solved a problem I had experienced repeatedly.

Do not add better performance, camera quality, accessories, or longer service life as reasons unless they are separately confirmed.

Natural closing line:

> Although I spent about 2,000 yuan more than I had planned, I think it was worth it because I no longer have to worry about running out of storage or constantly delete apps.

---

## 3. Cue Card B — OB15: Something you cannot live without

Do not take “cannot live without” literally. In IELTS, you can explain that it is something you **depend on heavily in everyday life**.

### What I use it for

- contacting family and friends
- studying and searching for information
- using maps and navigation
- making digital payments
- taking photos
- checking schedules or messages
- accessing useful apps
- dealing with small everyday tasks quickly

A natural line:

> I wouldn't say I literally couldn't survive without it, but it has become such an important part of my daily routine that life would be much less convenient without it.

---

## 4. Why it is essential

Do not just list functions. Group them into two or three larger ideas.

### Communication

> It is the main way I keep in touch with my family and friends.

### Study and information

> I use it to search for information, practise English, read messages, and deal with study-related tasks.

### Daily convenience

> It also works as my map, camera, payment tool, and access point for many services.

---

## 5. Balanced reflection

This makes the answer sound more mature.

Possible idea:

> I rely on my phone a lot, but I also think it is important not to become completely dependent on it. The phone is useful because it saves time and combines many tools in one device, but I still try not to use it when I need to concentrate.

# Core Story 008 — Boston: From a NeRF Project at MIT to a Celtics Game

## Why this is a core story

This Boston experience now has three concrete scenes and one clear reflection:

> short summer project at MIT → use NeRF to reconstruct 3D models from video → get up early for the final poster presentation → place second among groups with the same topic → watch the Celtics at TD Garden → revise my view of Boston → reflect on teamwork and balancing research with everyday life

It can answer the early-morning and live-sports questions without inventing a second trip. Boston is confirmed as my genuine favourite visited city. The NeRF branch may support a future technology or project question only after the exact smoothing method and result are confirmed.

---

## 1. Background

- I went to Boston for a short summer project at **MIT**.
- The project involved using **NeRF** technology to turn video footage into three-dimensional models.
- The reconstruction process produced visible noise or artifacts in the 3D models.
- My responsibility was to smooth the reconstructed models and reduce those artifacts.
- On the final day, our team presented the project with a poster and placed second among the groups working on the same topic.
- During the same stay, I watched an NBA game at **TD Garden**.

A concise non-technical explanation of the project:

> It was a short computer-vision project in which we used NeRF to reconstruct three-dimensional models from video footage.

---

## 2. The NeRF project scene

### Goal

- Use video footage as the input.
- Apply NeRF-related techniques to reconstruct a 3D model or scene.

### Problem

- The reconstructed models contained noise and visual artifacts.
- These artifacts made the surfaces look less clean or realistic.

### My responsibility

- I was responsible for smoothing the reconstructed models.
- The purpose was to reduce the visible noise and improve the quality of the final 3D result.

Natural IELTS wording:

> My main responsibility was dealing with the noise in the reconstructed models. I worked on smoothing the surfaces and reducing visual artifacts so that the final result would look cleaner.

Do not name a specific smoothing algorithm until it is confirmed.

---

## 3. Getting up early for the final presentation

- On the final day of the project, I needed to get up at **7:00 a.m.**.
- I normally got up at about **9:00 a.m.**, so this was early by my usual standard.
- Our team needed extra time to coordinate the presentation.
- We confirmed the division of speaking responsibilities and prepared the project poster.
- The presentation was completed successfully.
- Our team placed second among the groups working on the same project topic.
- I felt that all our work had been worthwhile and felt grateful to my teammates.

A concise version:

> On the final day, I got up at seven instead of my usual nine because our team needed to coordinate the presentation and prepare our poster. We eventually placed second among the groups working on the same topic, so I felt that the early start and all our effort had been worthwhile.

---

## 4. The Celtics game at TD Garden

- I watched an NBA game in person at **TD Garden**.
- The Boston Celtics played another NBA team, but I no longer remember the opponent.
- The opponent's name is not necessary for the story and should not be guessed.
- What impressed me most was the patience and support of the home crowd.
- When the Celtics were attacking, the audience shouted words such as **“Go, Celtics, go!”**
- When the team was defending, the crowd repeatedly shouted **“Defense!”** and created a very loud atmosphere.

The strongest scene:

> The most memorable part was not the final score. It was hearing the whole crowd change its chant with the game: they cheered for the Celtics on offense and shouted “Defense!” when the other team had the ball.

---

## 5. Change in my view of Boston

### Before

- I mainly associated Boston with universities, researchers, and a serious academic atmosphere.

### After the experience

- The Celtics game showed me a much more energetic and community-oriented side of the city.
- I began to see Boston as a place where academic life and ordinary leisure can exist together.
- The contrast between the MIT project and TD Garden made the city especially memorable.

### Personal reflection

This is a personal conclusion, not a universal claim about every researcher:

> The experience made me realize that research does not have to occupy every part of a person's life. Having interests outside work may help people protect their mental health, remain creative, and return to research with new energy.

---

## 6. Cue-card coverage

### PL06 — Your favorite city that you have visited

**Confirmed:** Boston is genuinely my favorite city among the cities I have visited, and it is the city I want to use for this cue card.

Focus on:

> summer project at MIT → original academic impression → Celtics game at TD Garden → energetic crowd → broader view of Boston → research-life balance

### EV07 — A live sports event you watched before

This route is now supported by enough real detail.

Focus on:

> NBA game → TD Garden → Celtics → opponent forgotten → offense and defense chants → supportive crowd → changed impression of the city

### EV11 - A time when you got up early

Focus on:

> final project day -> usual wake-up time 9:00 -> get up at 7:00 -> coordinate roles -> prepare poster -> successful presentation -> second place within the same project topic -> gratitude and worthwhile effort

The two-hour difference is sufficient because it is measured against my real routine.

### Technology or project topic

The NeRF branch can support a technology project or challenging technical problem:

> video input → NeRF reconstruction → noisy 3D model → responsible for smoothing and artifact reduction

Before using it for a full challenge question, confirm the method I used, whether I worked alone or with a team, and how much the final model improved.

### Other possible future uses

- a trip that changed my opinion of a place
- an experience that combined study and leisure
- a time I saw a lively crowd
- something that changed my view of work-life balance

# Core Story 009 - Jensen Huang and My Long-term AI Ambition

## Why this is a core story

This material connects one public figure with one genuine personal ambition:

> choosing a GPU for my first computer -> learning about Jensen Huang and NVIDIA -> respecting his long-term judgment on GPU computing, CUDA, and AI -> wanting to ask how he recognized that opportunity -> connecting the question to my own ambition to build a more advanced AI assistant

It can support four cue cards, but the spotlight must change for each one. It is not necessary to explain the technical project in detail during the exam.

---

## 1. How I learned about Jensen Huang

- I first became aware of NVIDIA when I needed to choose a GPU for my first personal computer.
- I later learned more about Jensen Huang through technology news and NVIDIA product launches or keynote presentations.
- I do not follow businesspeople closely, so this should not be presented as a lifelong admiration story.

A concise version:

> I first learned about Jensen Huang when I was choosing a GPU for my first computer, and I later saw more about him through technology news and NVIDIA keynote presentations.

---

## 2. Why I respect him and want to meet him

- He is a co-founder of NVIDIA and a well-known technology business leader.
- What I respect most is his long-term judgment and commitment to GPU computing, CUDA, and AI computing before their full commercial value became obvious.
- I would like to ask how he recognized the long-term potential of accelerated computing and maintained that strategy over time.
- This question matters to me because I also want to work in artificial intelligence and make sound long-term technical choices.

The central idea is **foresight and long-term judgment**, not company valuation alone.

A concise version:

> What I respect most is his long-term judgment. I would like to ask how he recognized the potential of GPU and AI computing before the opportunity became obvious to everyone.

---

## 3. My long-term ambition

- My long-term goal is to create an intelligent AI assistant with a **persistent internal affective state**.
- This state should influence the system's memory, judgment, and actions over time.
- The early inspiration came from watching **Iron Man** as a child and seeing JARVIS as more than a simple command-following tool.
- The idea became a serious long-term ambition around the beginning of university, approximately three years ago.
- What interests me most about AI is that models trained through prediction can display surprisingly complex abilities. This also gives us an engineering route for investigating how intelligence may arise.

A concise exam version:

> My long-term ambition is to build an AI assistant with a persistent internal affective state that can influence its memory, judgment, and actions, rather than one that only responds to individual commands.

---

## 4. Actions I have already taken

- I have studied artificial intelligence and model training.
- I have learned about agent architecture design.
- I have started a related GitHub project.
- The project is ongoing and unfinished.

This is enough detail for Part 2:

> I have studied model training and agent design, and I have also started a small ongoing GitHub project related to this idea.

The project name, architecture, and implementation details are not required unless a later cue card explicitly asks about a project.

---

## 5. Cue-card coverage

### PE02 - A successful business person you admire

Focus on:

> how I learned about Jensen Huang -> his role in NVIDIA -> long-term investment in GPU computing, CUDA, and AI -> why I respect that judgment

### PE12 - A famous person you would like to meet

Focus on:

> why I want to meet him -> the question I would ask -> how his answer could influence my own long-term decisions

### OB02 - An ambition that you have had for a long time

Focus on:

> childhood JARVIS inspiration -> ambition became serious at university -> functional idea for the assistant -> preparation already started

### OB14 - A perfect job you want to do in the future

Focus on:

> working in AI research and development -> interest in how intelligence arises -> building intelligent systems -> why the work suits my interests

---

## 6. Factual boundaries

- Do not claim that I know Jensen Huang personally or have followed his career for many years.
- Do not use NVIDIA's market value alone as proof of how he made individual strategic decisions.
- JARVIS is a fictional inspiration. My interpretation of the character is not evidence that JARVIS has a real affective architecture.
- Do not describe my GitHub project as a completed emotional AI assistant.
- Keep planned functions separate from functions that have already been implemented.

---

## 7. Useful vocabulary

- long-term judgment
- strategic foresight
- recognize the potential of a technology
- commit to long-term investment
- GPU computing
- accelerated computing
- product launch / keynote presentation
- a long-term ambition

- influence memory, judgment, and actions

# Core Story 010 - My Outgoing Childhood Friend

## Why this is a core story

The same real friend can support three person topics:

> primary-school friend -> long friendship and shared activities -> strong English-learning habits -> uses English confidently during an Oxford trip -> learns an error-notebook method from me -> improves his mathematics and physics grades

The person stays the same, but each cue card needs a different central event.

---

## 1. Friendship background

- We became friends in primary school.
- We studied together and often went out, ate, and shopped together.
- He is easy to talk to.
- Our personalities are different, which allows us to learn from each other.
- He is outgoing and willing to talk to other people, while I am more reserved.
- His willingness to try things has shown me that taking action can be better than simply waiting.

A concise description:

> I chose him because we have known each other since primary school and have shared many experiences. He is outgoing and willing to talk to people, while I am more reserved, so we often learn from each other.

---

## 2. English-learning ability

- He received high marks in English examinations.
- He did not rely only on textbooks.
- He used English-language music and films to notice how native speakers express themselves.
- His approach increased my own interest in learning English and influenced the way I studied it.

The strongest evidence is a real event during a trip to the United Kingdom:

- We were visiting the University of Oxford.
- We became separated from the leaders of our group.
- We did not know how to return to our hotel.
- He confidently asked an older local person for directions.
- The conversation helped us find our way back to the hotel.

A concise scene:

> When we became separated from our group at Oxford, he confidently asked a local person for directions and helped us find our way back to the hotel.

## 3. The skill he learned from me

- I was stronger in mathematics and physics, while he found these subjects more difficult.
- I explained how I used an error notebook and showed him my own notebook.
- The notebook recorded the questions I got wrong, the reasons for the mistakes, and the correct solutions.
- After seeing my method, he independently started keeping his own error notebooks.
- His grades in mathematics and physics improved.

### PE01 - A person who is good at learning and speaking new languages

Focus on:

> English exam performance -> music and films instead of textbooks alone -> Oxford problem -> natural communication with a local person -> successful result

> primary-school friendship -> shared study and leisure activities -> contrasting personalities -> Oxford scene -> what I learned from his willingness to act

### PE08 - One of your friends who learned a skill from someone

## 2. Why I want more memory

- I want to run small AI models locally.
- More memory would give me a wider choice of models for future projects.
- I do not currently have one specific model or project in mind.
- I also want to keep multiple web pages and applications open at the same time.
- My current computer slows down when I open too many applications or browser pages.

A concise explanation:

> I want 32 gigabytes of memory because it would let me run a wider range of small AI models locally while keeping several applications and browser pages open. My current computer becomes slow when I try to do too many of these things at once.

---

## 3. Why I want a MacBook Pro

- Portability is the main reason.
- I want a computer that I can carry with me throughout the day.
- I would use it in classrooms, laboratories, and libraries.
- I would also take it with me while travelling.

A concise version:

> I prefer a MacBook Pro because it is portable enough to carry between classrooms, laboratories, and libraries, and I could also take it with me when travelling.

---

## 4. How it would help me

- It would make multitasking smoother.
- It would reduce the slowdown caused by opening many applications and browser pages.
- It would expand the range of small local models available for future AI work.
- It would give me one portable machine for study, experiments, and travel.

A concise reflection:

> I do not need it for only one project. Its main value is that it would give me more options for future AI work while remaining portable enough for everyday study.

---

## 5. Cue-card route

### OB12 - A piece of technology, other than a phone, that you would like to own

Focus on:

> new MacBook Pro -> 32 GB memory -> not owned -> waiting for new model -> local small-model inference -> more model choices -> many pages and apps -> current slowdown -> portable -> classroom/lab/library/travel

---

## 6. Useful vocabulary

- a new MacBook Pro
- 32 gigabytes of memory
- wait for the next model
- run an AI model locally
- local model inference
- a wider range of small models
- keep multiple applications open
- multitask smoothly
- reduce slowdown
- carry it throughout the day
- a portable workstation
- support future projects

---

## 7. One-minute preparation keywords

> MacBook Pro -> 32 GB -> waiting for new model -> local inference -> more small-model choices -> many apps/pages -> current computer slows -> portable -> class/lab/library/travel -> future projects

---

## 8. Factual boundaries

- I do not own this MacBook Pro yet.
- Do not invent a chip, screen size, release date, price, or purchase deadline.
- I am waiting for a new model, but I have not committed to a specific unreleased configuration.
- I do not currently have one particular local model or project that I plan to run first.
- The benefit is greater flexibility for future projects, not a guaranteed performance claim about an unreleased device.

# Single-topic Card PL03 - A Friend's Apartment I Enjoyed Visiting but Would Not Live In

## Status

This is a verified personal material card for PL03. I enjoyed visiting my friend and playing games with him, but I would not want to live in his family's apartment.

---

- My friend and I arranged to spend time together.
- I went to his apartment to play video games with him.
- We played games such as **NBA 2K** and **FIFA**.
- The visit was enjoyable because I liked spending time and gaming with my friend.

A concise description:

> I once visited a friend's apartment because we had arranged to spend the day playing video games such as NBA 2K and FIFA. I enjoyed the visit because we had a good time together.

---

## 2. Who else was there

- My friend lived with his parents and younger brother.
- His parents and brother were at home during my visit.
- I did not know them well.
- I did not always know what to say to them and worried that my presence might disturb the family.

- This made the space feel cluttered rather than comfortable for me.

# IELTS Speaking Part 2 Knowledge Bank

**Purpose:** Collect flexible personal material before trying to produce a full two-minute answer.

## 状态定义

- **内容就绪**：真实事实足以回答题目，不需要在考场临时编造；可以开始一分钟准备和两分钟口述。
- **缺必要事实**：题目要求的关键事实仍缺失，现有素材只能作为候选，不能结算。
- **需要复习**：个人经历和影响真实，但作品或事件本身的内容记忆不足。
- **应急素材**：明确标记的合成场景，只在没有真实素材时使用，不得写入真实 Core Story。
- **口述已验证**：完成一分钟准备和两分钟口述后，未出现事实混淆、明显内容断裂或必须临场编造的情况。当前尚未给任何题目标记此状态。

# How to build each knowledge card

For every Part 2 topic, collect:

1. **Story title**
2. **Core change, event, person, place, object, or experience**
3. **Background**
4. **Cause or motivation**
5. **Specific actions**
6. **One memorable scene**
7. **Results**
8. **Feelings and reflection**
9. **Useful vocabulary and phrases**
10. **Other cue cards that can reuse the story**
11. **One-minute preparation keywords**

Do not write a full script first. Build the raw material, organise it, and then practise speaking from keywords.

# Core Story 001 — From Waiting to Taking Initiative

## Why this is a core story

This is **one personal experience that can answer several different IELTS Part 2 cue cards**. Do not memorize two separate answers.

The central story is:

> I used to be more passive and wait for opportunities or help to come to me. Around the end of my third year of college, I started to believe that I should take more initiative. One concrete change was the way I studied: instead of relying mainly on memorization, classes, and teachers, I began using AI actively as a personal study assistant, especially for IELTS speaking practice.

The facts stay mostly the same. **Only the spotlight changes according to the cue card.**

---

## Cue card A — Describe a change that you made recently

You should say:

- what the change was
- what caused the change
- what you did for the change
- how you feel about the change

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus mainly on the **study-routine change**.

- **Before:** I studied more passively, especially through vocabulary memorization, lectures, online courses, and material prepared by other people.
- **Change:** I began using AI actively as a learning assistant and added much more speaking practice.
- **Cause:** I needed a more efficient and personalized way to prepare for IELTS, and I had started to believe that I should take more initiative instead of waiting for the perfect learning environment.
- **Action:** I began having live English conversations, asking for explanations and corrections, building phrase and Part 2 story banks, and using AI to clarify difficult academic ideas.
- **Result:** My learning became more active, personalized, and efficient.

### Possible opening

> One important change I made recently was changing the way I study. I used to rely much more on passive learning, but now I try to take more initiative and use AI actively as a study partner.

---

## Cue card B — Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours

You should say:

- when you changed your opinion
- what your original opinion was
- why you changed it
- how you felt about the experience

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus mainly on the **mindset change**.

- **When:** Around the end of my third year of college.
- **Old opinion:** I believed that opportunities depended heavily on luck and coincidence, so I often waited for the right chance to appear.
- **Turning point:** I watched a one-hour Bilibili interview with research scientist Shunyu Yao. His account of continuing to learn, applying to companies, and sending out his CV showed me how people can actively create opportunities.
- **New opinion:** If I want something, I should at least try. Action can create choices that would not exist if I only waited.
- **Concrete proof of the new mindset:** I changed the way I studied. Instead of waiting for teachers, classes, or ideal conditions to solve my learning problems, I started using AI proactively and practising speaking more actively.

### Possible opening

> I used to believe that good opportunities would eventually come if I waited long enough, but around the end of my third year of college, I started to see things differently.

---

## Cue card C - EV06: An important decision you made in life

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus on the decision to stop waiting for ideal conditions and take greater responsibility for my own learning and opportunities.

- **Earlier mindset:** Opportunities seemed to depend mainly on luck or coincidence.
- **Decision:** I decided to take initiative and create more options through action.
- **Concrete action:** I changed the way I prepared for IELTS and began using AI actively for speaking practice, explanation, correction, and planning.
- **Importance:** The decision affected both my study behaviour and the way I think about future opportunities.

A concise opening:

> One important decision I made was to stop waiting for ideal opportunities and start taking more initiative in my own learning and future plans.

---

## Cue card D - EV08: A plan that you had to change recently

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus on a recent adjustment to my IELTS preparation plan.

- **Original plan:** Complete a fixed set of listening, reading, writing, and speaking tasks each day.
- **Problem:** In practice, one day's assigned workload took about two days to finish.
- **Reason for change:** The fixed daily schedule was creating backlog and did not reflect my actual working pace.
- **New plan:** Use a flexible priority system in which tasks can move forward or roll over according to progress.
- **Priority rule:** Speaking receives high priority because its preparation timeline is especially urgent, while the other skills remain in the plan.
- **Current status:** The revised plan is still being used, so do not claim a final score improvement yet.

A concise version:

> I originally followed a fixed daily IELTS schedule, but I found that one day's workload was taking me almost two days. I therefore changed it into a flexible, priority-based plan that allows unfinished tasks to roll over.

---

## Cue card E - OB03: Something that helped you learn a foreign language

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Use ChatGPT and live AI conversation as the concrete learning tool.

- I use it for IELTS speaking practice.
- I can ask it to repeat a question, slow down, or explain unfamiliar wording.
- I receive grammar and vocabulary corrections after speaking.
- I use it to organise a phrase bank and reusable Part 2 material.
- It turns passive vocabulary recognition into active retrieval and speaking practice.

A concise version:

> ChatGPT has helped me learn English by giving me frequent speaking practice, immediate explanations, and corrections that are adapted to my own mistakes.

---

## Cue card F - OB13: A program or app on your computer or phone

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus on ChatGPT as an application rather than describing artificial intelligence in general.

- I use it on a computer or phone.
- My main current use is personalised study, especially IELTS speaking.
- It helps me ask questions that I may hesitate to ask in a large class.
- It can explain the same idea in a different way when the first explanation is unclear.
- It reduces repetitive work when I organise notes and review errors.

A concise version:

> One application I use regularly is ChatGPT. I mainly use it as a study assistant because it lets me practise speaking, ask follow-up questions, and organise feedback around my own weaknesses.

---

## Cue card G - OB05: A TV show or online program you watched recently

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Use the full Bilibili interview rather than describing only one short clip.

- I watched it in **June**.
- It was approximately **one hour long**.
- The interviewee was research scientist **Shunyu Yao (姚顺雨)**.
- It covered his life and career journey from an undergraduate degree in physics to AI research.
- It also discussed his views on the current state and future development of artificial intelligence.
- The exact program title and channel have not been confirmed and should not be invented.

A concise version:

> In June, I watched a one-hour Bilibili interview with research scientist Shunyu Yao. It covered his transition from studying physics to working in AI research, as well as his views on the future of artificial intelligence.

---

## Cue card H - OB08: An interesting video

### Best spotlight for this cue card

Use the same interview, but focus on the part that changed my thinking.

- He described continuing to learn and sending his CV to different companies rather than waiting for an ideal opportunity.
- This made the idea of taking initiative feel concrete.
- It influenced how I approached my own learning and future choices.

A concise version:

> The most interesting part was hearing how he kept learning and applying for opportunities instead of simply waiting. It made me realise that action can create choices that would not otherwise exist.

---

## 1. Core story timeline

### Stage 1 — Before

- I was relatively passive about both opportunities and learning.
- I thought luck and coincidence were very important.
- In study, I relied heavily on memorizing vocabulary, lectures, online courses, and explanations from teachers.
- I sometimes knew a word when reading it but could not retrieve it quickly while speaking.
- Because I can be shy about asking questions, I did not always get the personal explanations I needed in a large class.

### Stage 2 — Turning point

- Near the end of my third year of college, I started thinking more seriously about my future.
- I noticed that classmates and other people often had more choices because they tried more things.
- In June, I watched a complete one-hour interview with Shunyu Yao on Bilibili.
- The program described his journey from studying physics as an undergraduate to becoming an AI research scientist and included his views on AI's current and future development.
- He also talked about continuing to learn, applying to companies, and sending out his CV instead of waiting for the perfect opportunity.
- That example made the idea of **taking initiative** feel concrete rather than abstract.

### Stage 3 — New mindset

> I used to believe that opportunities mainly came from luck, but now I think action creates opportunities.

Related ideas:

- Trying does not guarantee success, but not trying removes the possibility completely.
- Waiting can feel safe, but it can also make me passive.
- I should create more choices for myself instead of expecting choices to appear automatically.

### Stage 4 — Concrete behavior change: AI-assisted study

This is the strongest proof that the opinion change affected your real behavior.

- I stopped treating study as only memorization and passive input.
- I began practising spoken English in live AI conversations.
- I ask for questions to be repeated, slowed down, or explained in simpler language.
- I ask for grammar and vocabulary corrections after I speak.
- I build a phrase bank and a reusable Part 2 core-story bank.
- I use AI to clarify university material when a lecture or textbook explanation is not enough.
- I use AI to reduce repetitive work and make study time more efficient.

### Stage 5 - Recent adjustment to the IELTS plan

- The first plan assigned a fixed package of tasks to each day.
- My real pace showed that the workload was too rigid: one planned day took about two actual days.
- I changed to a priority-based plan rather than pretending the original schedule was still realistic.
- Tasks may be completed early or rolled forward when necessary.
- Speaking receives urgent attention, but listening, reading, and writing are not removed.

---

## 2. Memorable scenes

### Scene A — Shunyu Yao's Bilibili interview

> I remember watching a one-hour Bilibili interview in which research scientist Shunyu Yao described his transition from physics to AI and explained that he kept learning and applying for opportunities rather than simply waiting.

Use this scene when the question is about:

- changing an opinion
- inspiration
- social media
- a person who influenced you
- persistence
- career choices

### Scene B — AI speaking practice

> During an IELTS speaking practice session, I did not understand a cue-card word, so I asked the AI to slow down and explain it. After I understood the meaning, I was able to continue the answer instead of simply giving up.

Use this scene when the question is about:

- a recent change
- technology
- learning
- solving a problem
- communication
- becoming more independent

---

## 3. Results

### Practical results

- I can practise speaking more frequently.
- I receive feedback immediately.
- I have a more personalized study process.
- I can identify weak points instead of only repeating familiar material.
- I am training vocabulary retrieval, not only vocabulary recognition.
- I use study time more efficiently.

### Mindset results

- I am becoming more willing to take initiative.
- I am less likely to wait for the perfect condition before starting.
- I see action as a way to create possibilities.
- I feel more responsible for my own progress.

---

## 4. Feelings and reflection

Some feelings have not been fully confirmed yet, so keep this section flexible and only use wording that feels true in the exam.

Possible ideas:

- more motivated
- more independent
- more confident
- slightly nervous because taking action also means risking failure
- relieved because I no longer have to wait for perfect conditions
- more responsible for my own future

### Strong reflection

> Looking back, I realize that the biggest change was not simply using a new technology. It was becoming more proactive and taking greater responsibility for my own learning and opportunities.

---

## 5. Useful vocabulary

### Mindset and opportunities

- take initiative
- be proactive
- be passive
- create opportunities
- look for opportunities
- rely on luck
- coincidence
- turning point
- mindset
- step out of my comfort zone
- keep trying
- apply to a company
- send out a CV / résumé

### Learning and AI

- personalized learning
- active practice
- passive memorization
- immediate feedback
- retrieve vocabulary
- clarify a difficult concept
- identify weaknesses
- improve study efficiency
- learning assistant
- live conversation
- repetitive work

### Useful corrections

Say:

> AI has developed rapidly.

Not:

> AI grows fastly.

Say:

> improve my study efficiency

Not:

> improve my study quick

Say:

> If I don't try, the opportunity may never appear.

Not:

> If I not try, the choice will never be presented there.

Say:

> speak with an AI assistant in real time

or:

# Core Story 002 — Building a Line-Following Car as a Team

## 1. Core idea

During the last term, I worked in a four-person university team to build a small DIY car that could follow a line, use radar/sensors to detect obstacles, and move automatically. The project did not fully succeed, but it gives me a strong real story about teamwork, engineering, technical problems, imagination, time pressure, and learning from failure.

---

## 2. Background

- The project was part of a university course in the last term.
- The goal was to build a small autonomous car from scratch rather than simply copy an existing finished design.
- The car needed to follow a line and detect obstacles.
- There were four members in the team.

---

## 3. Team roles

The work was divided among the four members:

- one member designed the **radar / sensor PCB**;
- one member designed the **car-control PCB**, including the PID-control work;
- one member was responsible for the **lab notebook and final report**;
- my main responsibility was to **design and 3D-print the car structure and assemble the components**.

One teammate also coordinated the implementation plan:

- he planned how the team would build the car;
- he set project deadlines;
- he assigned the four main tasks to the team members;
- he regularly organised the work rather than making only one temporary plan.

### Useful simple IELTS version

> We divided the work according to different technical tasks, and my main responsibility was designing the car body, 3D-printing it, and assembling the components.

### The interface-board solution

After the radar PCB and car-control PCB had both been completed, connecting the two circuits became a problem. The teammate who organised the project proposed adding a small **interface board** between them. The team used this extra board, and it successfully solved the connection problem.

A concise version:

> When we had difficulty connecting the radar board to the car-control board, one teammate suggested adding a small interface board between them. His solution worked and allowed us to connect the two circuits successfully.

### Encouraging a teammate to redesign the control PCB

The teammate responsible for the car-control PCB and PID work fell behind schedule after several soldering attempts failed.

- I inspected the design and noticed that the PCB layout was too compact.
- The tight layout made the board difficult to solder and was a major reason for the repeated failures.
- I suggested changing both the PCB layout and the circuit connections.
- He initially disagreed because he had already invested substantial effort in the original design and did not want to lose that work.
- I used the repeated failures and the visible design problem as evidence that continuing with the same layout was unlikely to work.
- He eventually accepted the suggestion and changed the design.
- With the revised design, he successfully completed the task.
- He felt relieved, and I also felt relieved because the project could continue. I was proud that my technical judgment had proved correct.

A concise version:

> One teammate was reluctant to redesign his PCB because he had already invested a lot of work in it. I showed him that the layout was too compact and was causing repeated soldering failures. He eventually accepted my suggestion, changed the layout and connections, and completed the task successfully.

---

## 4. Main difficulty

The team faced several connected problems.

### Circuit and PCB delay

- Designing and producing the circuit board took longer than expected.
- Because of that delay, there was very little time left for PID testing and tuning.

### Mechanical problem

- The physical structure of the car also caused problems.
- The distance between the bottom of the car and the floor was too small.
- At times, the car did not move as expected because parts of the structure were too close to the ground.

### Control problem

- The PID parameters could not simply stay fixed.
- The team needed more time to test and adjust them under different conditions.
- Because testing time was limited, the final performance was unstable.

---

## 5. Result

- The project did **not fully succeed** in the final test.
- The failure was not caused by one single mistake.
- It came from several factors: circuit delays, limited testing time, mechanical design problems, and insufficient PID tuning.

This is useful for IELTS because the story does not need a perfect ending. The important part is explaining what happened and what I learned.

---

## 6. What I learned

- A technical project needs enough time for **integration and testing**, not only individual component design.
- Mechanical design, electronics, and control algorithms affect one another.
- A team can divide tasks, but members still need to communicate because one person's delay can affect everyone else's work.
- A failed result can still be valuable if I understand the causes and know what I would improve next time.

### Possible reflection

> Looking back, I realize that building each part separately was not enough. We also needed much more time to test how all the parts worked together.

---

## 7. Cue cards this story can cover

### Strong / already supported by the real experience

#### EV09 — A time when you worked in a group

Focus on:

> four members → different responsibilities → your 3D-printing and assembly role → technical problems → final result → teamwork lesson

#### EV05 — A challenging technological problem you faced

Focus on:

> DIY autonomous car → circuit delay → little testing time → mechanical/PID problems → attempted adjustments → what you learned

#### EV14 — A time when you used imagination

Focus on:

> no ready-made final design → designing the car structure → deciding how to arrange and assemble components → 3D printing → testing the physical design

#### PE06 — A person who gave a clever solution to a problem

Focus on:

> teammate who organised the project → two completed PCBs → connection problem → proposes an interface board → solution works

Keep the answer centred on the teammate and his reasoning rather than turning it into a general description of the whole project.

#### PE10 — A person who makes plans a lot

Focus on:

> teammate → implementation plan → deadlines → task allocation → radar board / control board / lab notebook / 3D car body → interface-board decision as evidence that he adjusted the plan when a new problem appeared

#### EV13 — A time when you encouraged someone to do something they didn't want to do

Focus on:

> control-board teammate → repeated soldering failures → compact PCB layout → sunk effort in original design → initially rejects redesign → I explain defect with evidence → changes layout and connections → task succeeds → mutual relief

Keep the roles clear: I encouraged the change, while my teammate was the person who initially did not want to redesign the board.

### Strong route

#### EV03 — A time when you received a message or email and it took you a long time to reply

**Status: content-ready.**

- Around six days before the deadline, the team was under heavy time pressure and spent most of the day working on the car.
- Because I was so focused on the project, I barely checked my phone.
- My mother sent me a routine message to check how I was doing.
- I did not reply for several days.
- When I eventually saw and answered the message, I apologised and explained that I had been busy with the project.

Natural version:

During that period, my mother sent me a routine message to ask how I was doing, but I did not reply for several days. When I finally answered, I apologised and explained why I had been so busy.

Do not invent the exact wording of either message.

# Core Story 003 — Reconnecting with Friends at Spider-Man: Brand New Day

## 1. Core idea

After not seeing some friends for a long time, we arranged an outing to watch **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** because we are all Marvel fans. I booked the tickets, and the new film gave us a natural chance to reconnect and enjoy being together again.

---

## 2. Background

- We had not met for quite a long time.
- We are all interested in Marvel movies and comics.
- In June, I saw a promotional clip for the film on Bilibili.
- When **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** came out, it gave us an easy reason to meet again.
- Because we already knew the characters and the Marvel universe well, we had plenty to talk about before and after the movie.

---

## 3. My role

- I helped turn the idea into an actual plan.
- I booked the movie tickets.
- The plan itself was simple, which made it easy for everyone to join.

A natural sentence:

> Since we hadn't seen each other in ages, we arranged to watch the new Spider-Man movie together, and I booked the tickets.

---

## 4. Vivid details

The strongest details are not complicated facts about the movie. They are the small interactions between friends.

- We talked about the characters because all of us were Marvel fans.
- After the movie, we discussed what we liked and how we would rate it.
- One friend thought it was the best film in the series.
- We also talked about future Marvel films we were looking forward to.
- The playful discussion made the outing feel more personal than simply sitting in a cinema.

A useful line:

> We ended up talking about the movie for quite a while, and one of my friends even said it was his favourite film in the series.

### The promotional clip with Messi

- The clip was an official advertisement for **Spider-Man: Brand New Day**.
- Lionel Messi appeared in it with Tom Holland's Spider-Man.
- The most memorable scene showed Spider-Man holding Messi while they swung between buildings on a web.
- Messi's facial expression looked stiff in this deliberately unusual acting situation.
- Some online viewers made jokes about his acting and said that he was not suited to being an actor.
- I found the scene funny rather than embarrassing.
- The unexpected crossover made me more interested in and excited about the film.

A concise description:

> In June, I saw a promotional clip for the film on Bilibili. The funniest scene showed Spider-Man holding Messi while they swung between buildings on a web. Messi looked unusually stiff, and many viewers joked about his acting. I found the crossover funny, and it made me look forward to the film even more.

The clip is listed as Sony Pictures Entertainment's *Super Fan Messi*. See the [published video listing](https://www.cinematoday.jp/video/VIYcDvJZBwDAmc).

---

## 5. Why I enjoyed the experience

Do not stop at:

> It improved our friendship.

Extend the idea in three layers:

### Reconnection

> We hadn't met for a long time, so the outing gave us a chance to reconnect.

### Feeling

> I felt relaxed and comfortable because I was spending time with people who shared the same interests.

### Small moment

> Our playful debate about the movie reminded me how much I had missed talking with them.

A natural combined version:

> What made the experience special was that we hadn't seen each other in ages. Watching the movie gave us a reason to meet again, but the part I enjoyed most was actually the conversation afterward. We joked about the characters, compared our opinions, and I realized how much I had missed spending time with them.

---

## 6. Result and reflection

- The outing helped us reconnect after a long period without meeting.
- It reminded me that friendships need some active effort to maintain.
- A simple shared interest can be enough to bring people together again.
- The experience was memorable mainly because of the people, not because the activity itself was unusual.

Possible reflection:

> Looking back, I realize that the movie was really just an excuse to meet. What mattered most was reconnecting with my friends.

---

# Core Story 004 — Ershou Lake: From a Polluted Lake to a Cleaner Public Place

## Why this is now a core story

This story has a clear **before-and-after change**, a real place, a family connection, a low-cost family outing, and a future-policy opinion. It is ready for EV02, OB09, and the main place routes.

The central chain is:

> Ershou Lake near my hometown → dirty and unpleasant in the past → local government introduced environmental measures and developed the area → the lake became cleaner and more attractive → more people started visiting → I now walk there with my family → I would support stricter anti-littering and ecosystem-protection rules

The confirmed local fact is that environmental cleanup or protection measures were introduced. Do not call those measures a named law. OB01 now uses a separate, officially verified plastic-shopping-bag regulation.

---

## 1. Background

- The lake is called **Ershou Lake** and is near my hometown.
- My grandparents used to go fishing there in the past.
- It was not a particularly famous place before.
- In the past, the lake was dirty and sometimes smelled unpleasant.
- Later, the local government introduced environmental cleanup or protection measures and developed the surrounding area for tourism.
- The area gradually became cleaner and more attractive to visitors.
- I now sometimes walk around the lake with my family.

---

## 2. The environmental change

### Before

- The lake looked less attractive.
- The water and surrounding environment were dirtier.
- There was an unpleasant smell.
- The area was not a major place for visitors.

### After

- Environmental cleanup and management improved the area.
- The lake became cleaner.
- Tourism and nearby commercial activity developed.
- More people began visiting the area.
- It became a more pleasant place for local families to walk and relax.

A natural sentence:

> One thing I've noticed is that the whole area has changed a lot. It used to be quite dirty and unpleasant, but after the local government introduced environmental measures, it gradually became much cleaner and more attractive.

---

## 3. Personal connection

This should not become only a general environmental-policy answer. Keep the story personal.

- My grandparents used to fish there.
- I now walk around the lake with my family.
- Walking there helps me relax and clear my mind.
- It gives me a chance to take my mind off study pressure.
- The change is easy for me to notice because I have a family connection with the place.

Possible line:

> What makes the change meaningful to me is that the lake is close to my hometown and my grandparents used to fish there, so it is not just a tourist attraction to me.

---

## 4. Boundary between the lake story and OB01

The cleanup of Ershou Lake is a real government action, but no official local legal title has been confirmed. Therefore:

- use this lake story for OB09, EV02, PL01, PL02, and PL04;
- use the separate plastic-shopping-bag card for OB01;
- never claim that a specific lake law caused the improvement.

---

## 5. Cue Card B — OB09: A new law you would like to introduce in your country

This is a **future proposal**, so keep it clearly separate from the existing cleanup measures.

### My proposed policy

I would like stricter rules around lakes and public waterways, especially:

- fines for people who throw rubbish into the lake or leave litter nearby
- stronger protection for the local ecosystem
- limits or controls on fishing practices if they damage fish populations or the balance of the ecosystem

A natural version:

> If I could introduce a new rule, I would make littering around lakes much more strictly controlled, with clear fines for people who throw rubbish into the water. I would also like stronger rules to protect fish and the wider ecosystem.

### Why I would introduce it

- Cleaning a lake once is not enough.
- The improved environment needs to be protected over time.
- More visitors can also create more rubbish and pressure on the ecosystem.
- Environmental protection works better when people know there are clear consequences for harmful behavior.

# Independent Card — OB01: Paid Use of Plastic Shopping Bags

## Why this is an independent card

This is a real national regulation selected for **OB01 — A law or regulation about environmental protection**. It is separate from the Ershou Lake story because the lake cleanup has no verified legal title.

The central chain is:

> national regulation → effective from 1 June 2008 → supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets → plastic shopping bags must be sold rather than given away → clear price → encourage people to use fewer bags → conserve resources and protect the environment

---

## 1. Verified facts

- The official Chinese title is **《商品零售场所塑料购物袋有偿使用管理办法》**.
- It was issued jointly by the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission, and the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce.
- It took effect on **1 June 2008**.
- It applies to retail venues including supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets.
- These retailers must charge consumers for plastic shopping bags and clearly display the price.
- They may not provide the bags free of charge or disguise a free bag through another promotion.
- The stated purpose is to conserve resources, protect the environment, and encourage consumers to use fewer plastic shopping bags.
- A later national measure effective in 2023 still requires retail businesses to follow this paid-use regulation.

---

## 2. Speakable English blocks

### Introduce the regulation

> I'd like to talk about China's regulation on the paid use of plastic shopping bags.

### Explain the rule

> It took effect in 2008 and requires supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets to charge customers for plastic shopping bags instead of giving them away for free.

### Explain the purpose

> Its main purpose is to reduce unnecessary use of plastic bags, conserve resources, and protect the environment.

### Explain why the design makes sense

> The rule does not completely ban plastic bags. Instead, it makes their cost visible, which can encourage shoppers to bring reusable bags or think twice before taking a new one.

---

## 3. Useful vocabulary

- paid use of plastic shopping bags
- charge customers for a bag
- provide something free of charge
- display the price clearly
- retail venue
- supermarket / shopping mall / open market
- reusable shopping bag
- reduce unnecessary consumption
- conserve resources
- plastic pollution
- environmental regulation

---

## 4. One-minute preparation keywords

> China → 2008 → paid plastic bags → supermarkets / malls / markets → no free bags → clear price → fewer unnecessary bags → reusable bags → resources + environment

---

## 5. Factual boundaries

- Call it a **regulation** or **administrative measure**, not necessarily a law passed by the legislature.
- Do not say China completely banned all plastic bags.
- The paid-use rule concerns plastic shopping bags supplied by retail venues. It excludes certain plastic pre-packaging bags used for hygiene and food-safety purposes, such as bags for loose fresh or cooked food.
- Do not connect this national regulation to the cleanup of Ershou Lake.

---

## 6. Official sources

- [国家发展改革委：《商品零售场所塑料购物袋有偿使用管理办法》](https://www.ndrc.gov.cn/xxgk/zcfb/fzggwl/200805/t20080528_960713.html) — official text, effective 1 June 2008.
- [商务部：《商务领域经营者使用、报告一次性塑料制品管理办法》](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zfxxgk/zc/gz/art/2024/art_7669e841461a4d73805e16f345e88579.html) — Article 9 continues to require retail operators to follow the paid-use regulation; effective 20 June 2023.

# Core Story 005 — My Sister's Education Decisions

## Why this is a core story

This card contains two real decisions involving the same family member. Use the university-choice event for **giving advice** and the later postgraduate-study decision for **feeling proud of a family member**. Do not merge the two timelines into one event.

The EV17 chain is:

> sister finishes an important exam → grades limit the available choices → she also has preferences about majors → my mother and I research universities with her → compare universities and majors → narrow down the options → help her make a final choice → feel relieved

The separate EV18 chain is:

> sister has a stable job → decides to leave it → pursues the postgraduate degree she genuinely wants → accepts uncertainty instead of staying only for security → I admire her courage and feel proud of her

Do not memorize a full answer. Memorize the decision-making process.

---

## 1. Background

- This happened several years ago when my sister needed to choose a university.
- Her exam results were an important factor because they affected which universities she could realistically apply to.
- She also had her own preferences about what subject or major she wanted to study.
- My mother and I helped her research the available choices.

---

## 2. What we actually did

- We searched online for universities that matched her grades.
- We looked at the majors available at different universities.
- We compared several options instead of choosing the first one we found.
- We considered both practical limits and her own interests.
- We discussed the advantages and disadvantages together.
- Finally, we helped her narrow the list down and make a decision.

A natural sentence:

> My mother and I helped my sister research different universities and compare the majors they offered, based on both her grades and what she was interested in.

---

## 3. Why this was real collaboration

This was not only one person giving help.

- My sister had to explain what she wanted.
- My mother and I helped collect and compare information.
- We discussed the options together.
- The final choice was made through a shared decision-making process.

This makes the story useful for a **working-with-a-family-member** question if that question appears in another speaking bank.

Possible line:

> We worked on it together because each of us contributed something different: my sister knew what she wanted, while my mother and I helped her compare the realistic options.

---

## 4. Strong route — EV17: A time when you gave advice to others

### Best spotlight

Focus on:

> sister needs to choose university → many options → research → compare majors and universities → give advice → final decision

### What the advice was

The advice was not simply:

> “Choose this university.”

It was more like:

> choose an option that matches both your academic results and your genuine interest in the subject.

Possible line:

> I tried not to make the decision for her. Instead, I helped her compare the choices and encouraged her to think about both the university and the major.

---

## 5. Strong route — EV18: A time when you felt proud of a family member

This is a separate, later decision from the university-choice event above.

- My sister had a stable job.
- She chose to give it up so that she could pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted.
- The decision meant leaving security behind and accepting uncertainty.
- I felt proud of her because she had the courage to choose the path she truly valued.

Natural IELTS wording:

> I felt proud of my sister when she gave up a stable job to pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted. I admired her courage because she was willing to leave a secure path and accept uncertainty for something that mattered to her.

Factual boundary:

- Do not claim that she completed the degree, entered a named programme, or achieved a particular result unless those facts are confirmed later.
- Do not present this as the result of the earlier university-choice discussion.

# Core Story 006 — Renhe Xincheng: A Convenient but Boring Shopping Center

## Why this is a core story

This is a real place near my home that can naturally cover three topics:

- **PL05 — A boring place**
- **PL07 — A tall building in your city you like or dislike**
- **PL08 — A shopping mall**

The central idea is not that the shopping center has nothing in it. In fact, it has many normal facilities. The reason I find it boring is that **the experience feels repetitive and not very innovative**.

The central chain is:

> shopping center near my home → clothes / coffee / food / cinema / promotions → I sometimes go with friends or family → every visit feels similar → nothing feels unique → convenient but boring

---

## 1. Basic background

- The shopping center is called **Renhe Xincheng**.
- It is near my home.
- It is a tall commercial building.
- Its exterior looks like an ordinary high-rise and has not left a distinctive visual impression on me.
- It has common facilities such as:
  - clothing shops
  - coffee shops
  - restaurants or food options
  - a cinema
- It sometimes has promotional activities or small events.

---

## 2. What I usually do there

### With friends

- I mainly go there to watch movies.
- The cinema is probably the main reason I visit with friends.

### With family

- I sometimes go there with my parents.
- We may have coffee or spend a little time there.

A natural sentence:

> I don't go there because I love shopping. Most of the time, I only go there to watch a movie with friends or have a coffee with my parents.

---

## 3. Why I find it boring

The problem is **not** that there are no activities.

The real problem is:

- the shops are very similar to those in many other malls
- the promotions feel repetitive
- there is not much that feels new or surprising
- most of the activities are things I could do in almost any shopping center
- after a short time, I feel there is nothing else I really want to explore

A strong natural explanation:

> Even though there are quite a few things to do, I still find it boring because every visit feels almost the same. The shops, promotions, and activities are quite predictable, so there is rarely anything that makes me curious or excited.

---

## 4. What an interesting shopping center should be like

This is a useful extension if you need more ideas.

For me, an interesting shopping center should:

- have something distinctive
- offer activities that are hard to find elsewhere
- change its events or exhibitions regularly
- give people a reason to visit beyond basic shopping, coffee, or movies

A natural line:

> Personally, I think a good shopping center should have something unique that makes people want to go there specifically, rather than offering the same things you can find everywhere else.

---

# Core Story 007 — My Smartphone: Expensive but Essential

## Why this is a core story

This is one real object that supports two cue cards:

- **OB10 — An item on which you spent more than expected:** content-ready.
- **OB15 — Something you cannot live without:** content-ready.

The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes:

- **OB10:** focus on the purchase, budget, and why the final cost was higher than expected.
- **OB15:** focus on how often you use the phone and why it has become essential in daily life.

The central chain is:

> previous 256 GB experience required deleting apps → planned to buy another 256 GB smartphone → changed to the 512 GB version at the time of purchase → paid about 2,000 yuan more → no longer worry about storage → worth the extra cost → use it every day

---

## 1. Basic background

- The object is my smartphone.
- My previous 256 GB phone often ran short of storage, so I regularly deleted apps that I did not use very often.
- I originally planned to buy the 256 GB version.
- At the time of purchase, I suddenly decided to buy the 512 GB version instead.
- The storage upgrade made the final cost higher than I had expected.
- After upgrading, I no longer needed to worry about storage space, so I felt the extra cost was worthwhile.
- Even so, I use it every day and depend on it for many practical tasks.

- With 512 GB, I no longer had to keep deleting less frequently used apps.
- I felt the extra cost was worthwhile because it solved a problem I had experienced repeatedly.
