# Core Story 008 — Boston: From a NeRF Project at MIT to a Celtics Game

## Why this is a core story

This Boston experience now has three concrete scenes and one clear reflection:

> short summer project at MIT → use NeRF to reconstruct 3D models from video → get up early for the final poster presentation → place second among groups with the same topic → watch the Celtics at TD Garden → revise my view of Boston → reflect on teamwork and balancing research with everyday life

It can answer the early-morning and live-sports questions without inventing a second trip. Boston is confirmed as my genuine favourite visited city. The NeRF branch may support a future technology or project question only after the exact smoothing method and result are confirmed.

---

## 1. Background

- I went to Boston for a short summer project at **MIT**.
- The project involved using **NeRF** technology to turn video footage into three-dimensional models.
- The reconstruction process produced visible noise or artifacts in the 3D models.
- My responsibility was to smooth the reconstructed models and reduce those artifacts.
- On the final day, our team presented the project with a poster and placed second among the groups working on the same topic.
- During the same stay, I watched an NBA game at **TD Garden**.

A concise non-technical explanation of the project:

> It was a short computer-vision project in which we used NeRF to reconstruct three-dimensional models from video footage.

---

## 2. The NeRF project scene

### Goal

- Use video footage as the input.
- Apply NeRF-related techniques to reconstruct a 3D model or scene.

### Problem

- The reconstructed models contained noise and visual artifacts.
- These artifacts made the surfaces look less clean or realistic.

### My responsibility

- I was responsible for smoothing the reconstructed models.
- The purpose was to reduce the visible noise and improve the quality of the final 3D result.

Natural IELTS wording:

> My main responsibility was dealing with the noise in the reconstructed models. I worked on smoothing the surfaces and reducing visual artifacts so that the final result would look cleaner.

Do not name a specific smoothing algorithm until it is confirmed.

---

## 3. Getting up early for the final presentation

- On the final day of the project, I needed to get up at **7:00 a.m.**.
- I normally got up at about **9:00 a.m.**, so this was early by my usual standard.
- Our team needed extra time to coordinate the presentation.
- We confirmed the division of speaking responsibilities and prepared the project poster.
- The presentation was completed successfully.
- Our team placed second among the groups working on the same project topic.
- I felt that all our work had been worthwhile and felt grateful to my teammates.

A concise version:

> On the final day, I got up at seven instead of my usual nine because our team needed to coordinate the presentation and prepare our poster. We eventually placed second among the groups working on the same topic, so I felt that the early start and all our effort had been worthwhile.

---

## 4. The Celtics game at TD Garden

- I watched an NBA game in person at **TD Garden**.
- The Boston Celtics played another NBA team, but I no longer remember the opponent.
- The opponent's name is not necessary for the story and should not be guessed.
- What impressed me most was the patience and support of the home crowd.
- When the Celtics were attacking, the audience shouted words such as **“Go, Celtics, go!”**
- When the team was defending, the crowd repeatedly shouted **“Defense!”** and created a very loud atmosphere.

The strongest scene:

> The most memorable part was not the final score. It was hearing the whole crowd change its chant with the game: they cheered for the Celtics on offense and shouted “Defense!” when the other team had the ball.

---

## 5. Change in my view of Boston

### Before

- I mainly associated Boston with universities, researchers, and a serious academic atmosphere.

### After the experience

- The Celtics game showed me a much more energetic and community-oriented side of the city.
- I began to see Boston as a place where academic life and ordinary leisure can exist together.
- The contrast between the MIT project and TD Garden made the city especially memorable.

### Personal reflection

This is a personal conclusion, not a universal claim about every researcher:

> The experience made me realize that research does not have to occupy every part of a person's life. Having interests outside work may help people protect their mental health, remain creative, and return to research with new energy.

---

## 6. Cue-card coverage

**Confirmed:** Boston is genuinely my favorite city among the cities I have visited, and it is the city I want to use for this cue card.

> summer project at MIT → original academic impression → Celtics game at TD Garden → energetic crowd → broader view of Boston → research-life balance

How to build each knowledge card

For every Part 2 topic, collect:

  1. Story title
  2. Core change, event, person, place, object, or experience
  3. Background
  4. Cause or motivation
  5. Specific actions
  6. One memorable scene
  7. Results
  8. Feelings and reflection
  9. Useful vocabulary and phrases
  10. Other cue cards that can reuse the story
  11. One-minute preparation keywords

Do not write a full script first. Build the raw material, organise it, and then practise speaking from keywords.

Core Story 001 — From Waiting to Taking Initiative

Why this is a core story

This is one personal experience that can answer several different IELTS Part 2 cue cards. Do not memorize two separate answers.

The central story is:

I used to be more passive and wait for opportunities or help to come to me. Around the end of my third year of college, I started to believe that I should take more initiative. One concrete change was the way I studied: instead of relying mainly on memorization, classes, and teachers, I began using AI actively as a personal study assistant, especially for IELTS speaking practice.

The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes according to the cue card.

Cue card A — Describe a change that you made recently

You should say:

  • what the change was
  • what caused the change
  • what you did for the change
  • how you feel about the change

Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus mainly on the study-routine change.

  • Before: I studied more passively, especially through vocabulary memorization, lectures, online courses, and material prepared by other people.
  • Change: I began using AI actively as a learning assistant and added much more speaking practice.
  • Cause: I needed a more efficient and personalized way to prepare for IELTS, and I had started to believe that I should take more initiative instead of waiting for the perfect learning environment.
  • Action: I began having live English conversations, asking for explanations and corrections, building phrase and Part 2 story banks, and using AI to clarify difficult academic ideas.
  • Result: My learning became more active, personalized, and efficient.

Possible opening

One important change I made recently was changing the way I study. I used to rely much more on passive learning, but now I try to take more initiative and use AI actively as a study partner.

Cue card B — Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours

You should say:

  • when you changed your opinion
  • what your original opinion was
  • why you changed it
  • how you felt about the experience

Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus mainly on the mindset change.

  • When: Around the end of my third year of college.
  • Old opinion: I believed that opportunities depended heavily on luck and coincidence, so I often waited for the right chance to appear.
  • Turning point: I watched a one-hour Bilibili interview with research scientist Shunyu Yao. His account of continuing to learn, applying to companies, and sending out his CV showed me how people can actively create opportunities.
  • New opinion: If I want something, I should at least try. Action can create choices that would not exist if I only waited.
  • Concrete proof of the new mindset: I changed the way I studied. Instead of waiting for teachers, classes, or ideal conditions to solve my learning problems, I started using AI proactively and practising speaking more actively.

Possible opening

I used to believe that good opportunities would eventually come if I waited long enough, but around the end of my third year of college, I started to see things differently.

Cue card C - EV06: An important decision you made in life

Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus on the decision to stop waiting for ideal conditions and take greater responsibility for my own learning and opportunities.

  • Earlier mindset: Opportunities seemed to depend mainly on luck or coincidence.
  • Decision: I decided to take initiative and create more options through action.
  • Concrete action: I changed the way I prepared for IELTS and began using AI actively for speaking practice, explanation, correction, and planning.
  • Importance: The decision affected both my study behaviour and the way I think about future opportunities.

A concise opening:

One important decision I made was to stop waiting for ideal opportunities and start taking more initiative in my own learning and future plans.

Cue card D - EV08: A plan that you had to change recently

Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus on a recent adjustment to my IELTS preparation plan.

  • Original plan: Complete a fixed set of listening, reading, writing, and speaking tasks each day.
  • Problem: In practice, one day's assigned workload took about two days to finish.
  • Reason for change: The fixed daily schedule was creating backlog and did not reflect my actual working pace.
  • New plan: Use a flexible priority system in which tasks can move forward or roll over according to progress.
  • Priority rule: Speaking receives high priority because its preparation timeline is especially urgent, while the other skills remain in the plan.
  • Current status: The revised plan is still being used, so do not claim a final score improvement yet.

A concise version:

I originally followed a fixed daily IELTS schedule, but I found that one day's workload was taking me almost two days. I therefore changed it into a flexible, priority-based plan that allows unfinished tasks to roll over.

Cue card E - OB03: Something that helped you learn a foreign language

Best spotlight for this cue card

Use ChatGPT and live AI conversation as the concrete learning tool.

  • I use it for IELTS speaking practice.
  • I can ask it to repeat a question, slow down, or explain unfamiliar wording.
  • I receive grammar and vocabulary corrections after speaking.
  • I use it to organise a phrase bank and reusable Part 2 material.
  • It turns passive vocabulary recognition into active retrieval and speaking practice.

A concise version:

ChatGPT has helped me learn English by giving me frequent speaking practice, immediate explanations, and corrections that are adapted to my own mistakes.

Cue card F - OB13: A program or app on your computer or phone

Best spotlight for this cue card

Focus on ChatGPT as an application rather than describing artificial intelligence in general.

  • I use it on a computer or phone.
  • My main current use is personalised study, especially IELTS speaking.
  • It helps me ask questions that I may hesitate to ask in a large class.
  • It can explain the same idea in a different way when the first explanation is unclear.
  • It reduces repetitive work when I organise notes and review errors.

A concise version:

One application I use regularly is ChatGPT. I mainly use it as a study assistant because it lets me practise speaking, ask follow-up questions, and organise feedback around my own weaknesses.

Cue card G - OB05: A TV show or online program you watched recently

Best spotlight for this cue card

Use the full Bilibili interview rather than describing only one short clip.

  • I watched it in June.

Core Story 002 — Building a Line-Following Car as a Team

1. Core idea

During the last term, I worked in a four-person university team to build a small DIY car that could follow a line, use radar/sensors to detect obstacles, and move automatically. The project did not fully succeed, but it gives me a strong real story about teamwork, engineering, technical problems, imagination, time pressure, and learning from failure.

2. Background

  • The project was part of a university course in the last term.
  • The goal was to build a small autonomous car from scratch rather than simply copy an existing finished design.
  • The car needed to follow a line and detect obstacles.
  • There were four members in the team.

3. Team roles

The work was divided among the four members:

  • one member designed the radar / sensor PCB;
  • one member designed the car-control PCB, including the PID-control work;
  • one member was responsible for the lab notebook and final report;
  • my main responsibility was to design and 3D-print the car structure and assemble the components.

One teammate also coordinated the implementation plan:

  • he planned how the team would build the car;
  • he set project deadlines;
  • he assigned the four main tasks to the team members;
  • he regularly organised the work rather than making only one temporary plan.

Useful simple IELTS version

We divided the work according to different technical tasks, and my main responsibility was designing the car body, 3D-printing it, and assembling the components.

The interface-board solution

After the radar PCB and car-control PCB had both been completed, connecting the two circuits became a problem. The teammate who organised the project proposed adding a small interface board between them. The team used this extra board, and it successfully solved the connection problem.

A concise version:

When we had difficulty connecting the radar board to the car-control board, one teammate suggested adding a small interface board between them. His solution worked and allowed us to connect the two circuits successfully.

Encouraging a teammate to redesign the control PCB

The teammate responsible for the car-control PCB and PID work fell behind schedule after several soldering attempts failed.

  • I inspected the design and noticed that the PCB layout was too compact.
  • The tight layout made the board difficult to solder and was a major reason for the repeated failures.
  • I suggested changing both the PCB layout and the circuit connections.
  • He initially disagreed because he had already invested substantial effort in the original design and did not want to lose that work.
  • I used the repeated failures and the visible design problem as evidence that continuing with the same layout was unlikely to work.
  • He eventually accepted the suggestion and changed the design.
  • With the revised design, he successfully completed the task.
  • He felt relieved, and I also felt relieved because the project could continue. I was proud that my technical judgment had proved correct.

A concise version:

One teammate was reluctant to redesign his PCB because he had already invested a lot of work in it. I showed him that the layout was too compact and was causing repeated soldering failures. He eventually accepted my suggestion, changed the layout and connections, and completed the task successfully.

4. Main difficulty

The team faced several connected problems.

Circuit and PCB delay

  • Designing and producing the circuit board took longer than expected.
  • Because of that delay, there was very little time left for PID testing and tuning.

Mechanical problem

  • The physical structure of the car also caused problems.
  • The distance between the bottom of the car and the floor was too small.
  • At times, the car did not move as expected because parts of the structure were too close to the ground.

Control problem

  • The PID parameters could not simply stay fixed.
  • The team needed more time to test and adjust them under different conditions.
  • Because testing time was limited, the final performance was unstable.

5. Result

  • The project did not fully succeed in the final test.
  • The failure was not caused by one single mistake.
  • It came from several factors: circuit delays, limited testing time, mechanical design problems, and insufficient PID tuning.

This is useful for IELTS because the story does not need a perfect ending. The important part is explaining what happened and what I learned.

6. What I learned

  • A technical project needs enough time for integration and testing, not only individual component design.
  • Mechanical design, electronics, and control algorithms affect one another.
  • A team can divide tasks, but members still need to communicate because one person's delay can affect everyone else's work.
  • A failed result can still be valuable if I understand the causes and know what I would improve next time.

Possible reflection

Looking back, I realize that building each part separately was not enough. We also needed much more time to test how all the parts worked together.

After not seeing some friends for a long time, we arranged an outing to watch Spider-Man: Brand New Day because we are all Marvel fans. I booked the tickets, and the new film gave us a natural chance to reconnect and enjoy being together again.

  • I helped turn the idea into an actual plan.

Why this is now a core story

This story has a clear before-and-after change, a real place, a family connection, a low-cost family outing, and a future-policy opinion. It is ready for EV02, OB09, and the main place routes.

The central chain is:

Ershou Lake near my hometown → dirty and unpleasant in the past → local government introduced environmental measures and developed the area → the lake became cleaner and more attractive → more people started visiting → I now walk there with my family → I would support stricter anti-littering and ecosystem-protection rules

The confirmed local fact is that environmental cleanup or protection measures were introduced. Do not call those measures a named law. OB01 now uses a separate, officially verified plastic-shopping-bag regulation.

1. Background

  • The lake is called Ershou Lake and is near my hometown.
  • My grandparents used to go fishing there in the past.
  • It was not a particularly famous place before.
  • In the past, the lake was dirty and sometimes smelled unpleasant.
  • Later, the local government introduced environmental cleanup or protection measures and developed the surrounding area for tourism.
  • The area gradually became cleaner and more attractive to visitors.
  • I now sometimes walk around the lake with my family.

2. The environmental change

Before

  • The lake looked less attractive.
  • The water and surrounding environment were dirtier.
  • There was an unpleasant smell.
  • The area was not a major place for visitors.

After

  • Environmental cleanup and management improved the area.
  • The lake became cleaner.
  • Tourism and nearby commercial activity developed.
  • More people began visiting the area.
  • It became a more pleasant place for local families to walk and relax.

This should not become only a general environmental-policy answer. Keep the story personal.

  • My grandparents used to fish there.
  • I now walk around the lake with my family.
  • Walking there helps me relax and clear my mind.
  • It gives me a chance to take my mind off study pressure.
  • The change is easy for me to notice because I have a family connection with the place.

Possible line:

What makes the change meaningful to me is that the lake is close to my hometown and my grandparents used to fish there, so it is not just a tourist attraction to me.

4. Boundary between the lake story and OB01

The cleanup of Ershou Lake is a real government action, but no official local legal title has been confirmed. Therefore:

  • use the separate plastic-shopping-bag card for OB01;

  • stronger protection for the local ecosystem
  • limits or controls on fishing practices if they damage fish populations or the balance of the ecosystem

A natural version:

If I could introduce a new rule, I would make littering around lakes much more strictly controlled, with clear fines for people who throw rubbish into the water. I would also like stronger rules to protect fish and the wider ecosystem.

Why I would introduce it

  • Cleaning a lake once is not enough.
  • The improved environment needs to be protected over time.
  • More visitors can also create more rubbish and pressure on the ecosystem.

Independent Card — OB01: Paid Use of Plastic Shopping Bags

Why this is an independent card

This is a real national regulation selected for OB01 — A law or regulation about environmental protection. It is separate from the Ershou Lake story because the lake cleanup has no verified legal title.

The central chain is:

national regulation → effective from 1 June 2008 → supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets → plastic shopping bags must be sold rather than given away → clear price → encourage people to use fewer bags → conserve resources and protect the environment

1. Verified facts

  • The official Chinese title is 《商品零售场所塑料购物袋有偿使用管理办法》.
  • It was issued jointly by the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission, and the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce.
  • It took effect on 1 June 2008.
  • It applies to retail venues including supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets.
  • These retailers must charge consumers for plastic shopping bags and clearly display the price.
  • They may not provide the bags free of charge or disguise a free bag through another promotion.
  • The stated purpose is to conserve resources, protect the environment, and encourage consumers to use fewer plastic shopping bags.
  • A later national measure effective in 2023 still requires retail businesses to follow this paid-use regulation.

2. Speakable English blocks

Introduce the regulation

I'd like to talk about China's regulation on the paid use of plastic shopping bags.

Explain the rule

It took effect in 2008 and requires supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets to charge customers for plastic shopping bags instead of giving them away for free.

Explain the purpose

Its main purpose is to reduce unnecessary use of plastic bags, conserve resources, and protect the environment.

Explain why the design makes sense

The rule does not completely ban plastic bags. Instead, it makes their cost visible, which can encourage shoppers to bring reusable bags or think twice before taking a new one.

3. Useful vocabulary

  • paid use of plastic shopping bags
  • charge customers for a bag
  • provide something free of charge
  • display the price clearly
  • retail venue
  • supermarket / shopping mall / open market
  • reusable shopping bag
  • reduce unnecessary consumption
  • conserve resources
  • plastic pollution
  • environmental regulation

4. One-minute preparation keywords

China → 2008 → paid plastic bags → supermarkets / malls / markets → no free bags → clear price → fewer unnecessary bags → reusable bags → resources + environment

5. Factual boundaries

  • Call it a regulation or administrative measure, not necessarily a law passed by the legislature.
  • Do not say China completely banned all plastic bags.
  • The paid-use rule concerns plastic shopping bags supplied by retail venues. It excludes certain plastic pre-packaging bags used for hygiene and food-safety purposes, such as bags for loose fresh or cooked food.
  • Do not connect this national regulation to the cleanup of Ershou Lake.

6. Official sources

  • 国家发展改革委：《商品零售场所塑料购物袋有偿使用管理办法》 — official text, effective 1 June 2008.
  • 商务部：《商务领域经营者使用、报告一次性塑料制品管理办法》 — Article 9 continues to require retail operators to follow the paid-use regulation; effective 20 June 2023.

Core Story 005 — My Sister's Education Decisions

Why this is a core story

This card contains two real decisions involving the same family member. Use the university-choice event for giving advice and the later postgraduate-study decision for feeling proud of a family member. Do not merge the two timelines into one event.

The EV17 chain is:

sister finishes an important exam → grades limit the available choices → she also has preferences about majors → my mother and I research universities with her → compare universities and majors → narrow down the options → help her make a final choice → feel relieved

The separate EV18 chain is:

sister has a stable job → decides to leave it → pursues the postgraduate degree she genuinely wants → accepts uncertainty instead of staying only for security → I admire her courage and feel proud of her

Do not memorize a full answer. Memorize the decision-making process.

1. Background

  • This happened several years ago when my sister needed to choose a university.
  • Her exam results were an important factor because they affected which universities she could realistically apply to.
  • She also had her own preferences about what subject or major she wanted to study.
  • My mother and I helped her research the available choices.

2. What we actually did

  • We searched online for universities that matched her grades.
  • We looked at the majors available at different universities.
  • We compared several options instead of choosing the first one we found.
  • We considered both practical limits and her own interests.
  • We discussed the advantages and disadvantages together.
  • Finally, we helped her narrow the list down and make a decision.

A natural sentence:

My mother and I helped my sister research different universities and compare the majors they offered, based on both her grades and what she was interested in.

3. Why this was real collaboration

This was not only one person giving help.

  • My sister had to explain what she wanted.
  • My mother and I helped collect and compare information.
  • We discussed the options together.
  • The final choice was made through a shared decision-making process.

This makes the story useful for a working-with-a-family-member question if that question appears in another speaking bank.

Possible line:

We worked on it together because each of us contributed something different: my sister knew what she wanted, while my mother and I helped her compare the realistic options.

4. Strong route — EV17: A time when you gave advice to others

Best spotlight

Focus on:

sister needs to choose university → many options → research → compare majors and universities → give advice → final decision

What the advice was

The advice was not simply:

“Choose this university.”

It was more like:

choose an option that matches both your academic results and your genuine interest in the subject.

Possible line:

I tried not to make the decision for her. Instead, I helped her compare the choices and encouraged her to think about both the university and the major.

5. Strong route — EV18: A time when you felt proud of a family member

This is a separate, later decision from the university-choice event above.

  • My sister had a stable job.
  • She chose to give it up so that she could pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted.
  • The decision meant leaving security behind and accepting uncertainty.
  • I felt proud of her because she had the courage to choose the path she truly valued.

Natural IELTS wording:

I felt proud of my sister when she gave up a stable job to pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted. I admired her courage because she was willing to leave a secure path and accept uncertainty for something that mattered to her.

Factual boundary:

  • Do not claim that she completed the degree, entered a named programme, or achieved a particular result unless those facts are confirmed later.
  • Do not present this as the result of the earlier university-choice discussion.

6. Family-help route

This story can also support questions about helping a family member.

Focus on:

important decision → she needed information → we researched together → I explained or compared options → she became more confident about the choice

Possible line:

I wanted to help because choosing a university can affect several years of someone's life, so I felt it was worth spending time on the decision.

Core Story 006 — Renhe Xincheng: A Convenient but Boring Shopping Center

Why this is a core story

This is a real place near my home that can naturally cover three topics:

  • PL05 — A boring place
  • PL07 — A tall building in your city you like or dislike
  • PL08 — A shopping mall

The central idea is not that the shopping center has nothing in it. In fact, it has many normal facilities. The reason I find it boring is that the experience feels repetitive and not very innovative.

The central chain is:

shopping center near my home → clothes / coffee / food / cinema / promotions → I sometimes go with friends or family → every visit feels similar → nothing feels unique → convenient but boring

1. Basic background

  • The shopping center is called Renhe Xincheng.
  • It is near my home.
  • It is a tall commercial building.
  • Its exterior looks like an ordinary high-rise and has not left a distinctive visual impression on me.
  • It has common facilities such as:
    • clothing shops
    • coffee shops
    • restaurants or food options
    • a cinema
  • It sometimes has promotional activities or small events.

2. What I usually do there

With friends

  • I mainly go there to watch movies.
  • The cinema is probably the main reason I visit with friends.

With family

  • I sometimes go there with my parents.
  • We may have coffee or spend a little time there.

A natural sentence:

I don't go there because I love shopping. Most of the time, I only go there to watch a movie with friends or have a coffee with my parents.

3. Why I find it boring

The problem is not that there are no activities.

The real problem is:

  • the shops are very similar to those in many other malls
  • the promotions feel repetitive
  • there is not much that feels new or surprising
  • most of the activities are things I could do in almost any shopping center
  • after a short time, I feel there is nothing else I really want to explore

A strong natural explanation:

Even though there are quite a few things to do, I still find it boring because every visit feels almost the same. The shops, promotions, and activities are quite predictable, so there is rarely anything that makes me curious or excited.

This is a useful extension if you need more ideas.

For me, an interesting shopping center should:

  • have something distinctive
  • offer activities that are hard to find elsewhere
  • change its events or exhibitions regularly
  • give people a reason to visit beyond basic shopping, coffee, or movies

A natural line:

Personally, I think a good shopping center should have something unique that makes people want to go there specifically, rather than offering the same things you can find everywhere else.

Core Story 008 — Boston: From a NeRF Project at MIT to a Celtics Game

Why this is a core story

This Boston experience now has three concrete scenes and one clear reflection:

short summer project at MIT → use NeRF to reconstruct 3D models from video → get up early for the final poster presentation → place second among groups with the same topic → watch the Celtics at TD Garden → revise my view of Boston → reflect on teamwork and balancing research with everyday life

It can answer the early-morning and live-sports questions without inventing a second trip. Boston is confirmed as my genuine favourite visited city. The NeRF branch may support a future technology or project question only after the exact smoothing method and result are confirmed.

1. Background

  • I went to Boston for a short summer project at MIT.
  • The project involved using NeRF technology to turn video footage into three-dimensional models.
  • The reconstruction process produced visible noise or artifacts in the 3D models.
  • My responsibility was to smooth the reconstructed models and reduce those artifacts.
  • On the final day, our team presented the project with a poster and placed second among the groups working on the same topic.
  • During the same stay, I watched an NBA game at TD Garden.

A concise non-technical explanation of the project:

It was a short computer-vision project in which we used NeRF to reconstruct three-dimensional models from video footage.

2. The NeRF project scene

Goal

  • Use video footage as the input.
  • Apply NeRF-related techniques to reconstruct a 3D model or scene.

Problem

  • The reconstructed models contained noise and visual artifacts.
  • These artifacts made the surfaces look less clean or realistic.

My responsibility

  • I was responsible for smoothing the reconstructed models.
  • The purpose was to reduce the visible noise and improve the quality of the final 3D result.

Natural IELTS wording:

My main responsibility was dealing with the noise in the reconstructed models. I worked on smoothing the surfaces and reducing visual artifacts so that the final result would look cleaner.

Do not name a specific smoothing algorithm until it is confirmed.

3. Getting up early for the final presentation

  • On the final day of the project, I needed to get up at 7:00 a.m..
  • I normally got up at about 9:00 a.m., so this was early by my usual standard.
  • Our team needed extra time to coordinate the presentation.
  • We confirmed the division of speaking responsibilities and prepared the project poster.
  • The presentation was completed successfully.
  • Our team placed second among the groups working on the same project topic.
  • I felt that all our work had been worthwhile and felt grateful to my teammates.

A concise version:

On the final day, I got up at seven instead of my usual nine because our team needed to coordinate the presentation and prepare our poster. We eventually placed second among the groups working on the same topic, so I felt that the early start and all our effort had been worthwhile.

4. The Celtics game at TD Garden

  • I watched an NBA game in person at TD Garden.
  • The Boston Celtics played another NBA team, but I no longer remember the opponent.
  • The opponent's name is not necessary for the story and should not be guessed.
  • What impressed me most was the patience and support of the home crowd.
  • When the Celtics were attacking, the audience shouted words such as “Go, Celtics, go!”
  • When the team was defending, the crowd repeatedly shouted “Defense!” and created a very loud atmosphere.

The strongest scene:

The most memorable part was not the final score. It was hearing the whole crowd change its chant with the game: they cheered for the Celtics on offense and shouted “Defense!” when the other team had the ball.

5. Change in my view of Boston

Before

  • I mainly associated Boston with universities, researchers, and a serious academic atmosphere.

After the experience

  • The Celtics game showed me a much more energetic and community-oriented side of the city.
  • I began to see Boston as a place where academic life and ordinary leisure can exist together.
  • The contrast between the MIT project and TD Garden made the city especially memorable.

Personal reflection

This is a personal conclusion, not a universal claim about every researcher:

The experience made me realize that research does not have to occupy every part of a person's life. Having interests outside work may help people protect their mental health, remain creative, and return to research with new energy.

summer project at MIT → original academic impression → Celtics game at TD Garden → energetic crowd → broader view of Boston → research-life balance

  • I wanted to give up many times during this process.
  • The book's message about persistence encouraged me to continue.
  • I eventually completed the mechanical model, the parts fitted together successfully, and the car could perform basic movement.
  • This local mechanical result is separate from the complete line-following, obstacle-avoidance, and PID evaluation, which did not fully succeed.

A concise scene:

In the end, the mechanical structure was assembled successfully and the car could perform basic movement.

3. Why the story still matters to me

  • I do not value the book because I can retell every event in it.
  • I value it because one simple idea from childhood continued to affect my behaviour years later.
  • The car project turned the book's lesson from an abstract message into a real experience.

A concise reflection:

What makes the story meaningful to me is that its lesson did not remain in the book. Years later, it helped me persist with a frustrating engineering task until I completed it.

The official synopsis provides this short, accurate sequence:

  • Sultan Leo the Twenty-eighth invites the animals to his wedding on a flower-covered meadow.
  • The tortoise Tranquilla sets out on the long journey because she wants to attend.
  • Other animals laugh at her and doubt that such a slow animal can arrive in time.
  • She continues slowly, step by step, for months and years.
  • She eventually reaches the decorated meadow and finds that a wedding is taking place.
  • It is now the wedding of Leo the Twenty-ninth rather than Leo the Twenty-eighth, but her persistence has still carried her to the destination.

The story is about a tortoise called Tranquilla who sets out for a lion's wedding. Other animals laugh at her because she moves so slowly, but she keeps going step by step for months and years. Core Story 001 — From Waiting to Taking Initiative Why this is a core story This is one personal experience that can answer several different IELTS Part 2 cue cards. Do not memorize two separate answers. The central story is: I used to be more passive and wait for opportunities or help to come to me. Around the end of my third year of college, I started to believe that I should take more initiative. One concrete change was the way I studied: instead of relying mainly on memorization, classes, and teachers, I began using AI actively as a personal study assistant, especially for IELTS speaking practice. The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes according to the cue card. Cue card A — Describe a change that you made recently You should say: what the change was what caused the change what you did for the change how you feel about the change Best spotlight for this cue card Focus mainly on the study-routine change. Before: I studied more passively, especially through vocabulary memorization, lectures, online courses, and material prepared by other people. Change: I began using AI actively as a learning assistant and added much more speaking practice. Cause: I needed a more efficient and personalized way to prepare for IELTS, and I had started to believe that I should take more initiative instead of waiting for the perfect learning environment. Action: I began having live English conversations, asking for explanations and corrections, building phrase and Part 2 story banks, and using AI to clarify difficult academic ideas. Result: My learning became more active, personalized, and efficient. Possible opening One important change I made recently was changing the way I study. I used to rely much more on passive learning, but now I try to take more initiative and use AI actively as a study partner. Cue card B — Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours You should say: when you changed your opinion what your original opinion was why you changed it how you felt about the experience Best spotlight for this cue card Focus mainly on the mindset change. When: Around the end of my third year of college. Old opinion: I believed that opportunities depended heavily on luck and coincidence, so I often waited for the right chance to appear. Turning point: I watched a one-hour Bilibili interview with research scientist Shunyu Yao. His account of continuing to learn, applying to companies, and sending out his CV showed me how people can actively create opportunities. New opinion: If I want something, I should at least try. Action can create choices that would not exist if I only waited. Concrete proof of the new mindset: I changed the way I studied. Instead of waiting for teachers, classes, or ideal conditions to solve my learning problems, I started using AI proactively and practising speaking more actively. Possible opening I used to believe that good opportunities would eventually come if I waited long enough, but around the end of my third year of college, I started to see things differently. Cue card C - EV06: An important decision you made in life Best spotlight for this cue card Focus on the decision to stop waiting for ideal conditions and take greater responsibility for my own learning and opportunities. Earlier mindset: Opportunities seemed to depend mainly on luck or coincidence. Decision: I decided to take initiative and create more options through action. Concrete action: I changed the way I prepared for IELTS and began using AI actively for speaking practice, explanation, correction, and planning. Importance: The decision affected both my study behaviour and the way I think about future opportunities. One academic subject where AI gave you a particularly useful explanation. Core Story 002 — Building a Line-Following Car as a Team 1. Core idea During the last term, I worked in a four-person university team to build a small DIY car that could follow a line, use radar/sensors to detect obstacles, and move automatically. The project did not fully succeed, but it gives me a strong real story about teamwork, engineering, technical problems, imagination, time pressure, and learning from failure. 2. Background The project was part of a university course in the last term. The goal was to build a small autonomous car from scratch rather than simply copy an existing finished design. The car needed to follow a line and detect obstacles. There were four members in the team. 3. Team roles The work was divided among the four members: one member designed the radar / sensor PCB; one member designed the car-control PCB, including the PID-control work; one member was responsible for the lab notebook and final report; my main responsibility was to design and 3D-print the car structure and assemble the components. One teammate also coordinated the implementation plan: he planned how the team would build the car; he set project deadlines; he assigned the four main tasks to the team members; he regularly organised the work rather than making only one temporary plan. Useful simple IELTS version We divided the work according to different technical tasks, and my main responsibility was designing the car body, 3D-printing it, and assembling the components. The interface-board solution After the radar PCB and car-control PCB had both been completed, connecting the two circuits became a problem. The teammate who organised the project proposed adding a small interface board between them. The team used this extra board, and it successfully solved the connection problem. A concise version: When we had difficulty connecting the radar board to the car-control board, one teammate suggested adding a small interface board between them. His solution worked and allowed us to connect the two circuits successfully. Encouraging a teammate to redesign the control PCB The teammate responsible for the car-control PCB and PID work fell behind schedule after several soldering attempts failed. I inspected the design and noticed that the PCB layout was too compact. The tight layout made the board difficult to solder and was a major reason for the repeated failures. I suggested changing both the PCB layout and the circuit connections. He initially disagreed because he had already invested substantial effort in the original design and did not want to lose that work. I used the repeated failures and the visible design problem as evidence that continuing with the same layout was unlikely to work. He eventually accepted the suggestion and changed the design. With the revised design, he successfully completed the task. He felt relieved, and I also felt relieved because the project could continue. I was proud that my technical judgment had proved correct. A concise version: One teammate was reluctant to redesign his PCB because he had already invested a lot of work in it. I showed him that the layout was too compact and was causing repeated soldering failures. He eventually accepted my suggestion, changed the layout and connections, and completed the task successfully. 4. Main difficulty The team faced several connected problems. Circuit and PCB delay Designing and producing the circuit board took longer than expected. Because of that delay, there was very little time left for PID testing and tuning. Mechanical problem The physical structure of the car also caused problems. The distance between the bottom of the car and the floor was too small. At times, the car did not move as expected because parts of the structure were too close to the ground. Control problem The PID parameters could not simply stay fixed. The team needed more time to test and adjust them under different conditions. Because testing time was limited, the final performance was unstable. 5. Result The project did not fully succeed in the final test. The failure was not caused by one single mistake. It came from several factors: circuit delays, limited testing time, mechanical design problems, and insufficient PID tuning. This is useful for IELTS because the story does not need a perfect ending. The important part is explaining what happened and what I learned. 6. What I learned A technical project needs enough time for integration and testing, not only individual component design. Mechanical design, electronics, and control algorithms affect one another. A team can divide tasks, but members still need to communicate because one person's delay can affect everyone else's work. A failed result can still be valuable if I understand the causes and know what I would improve next time. Possible reflection Looking back, I realize that building each part separately was not enough. We also needed much more time to test how all the parts worked together. 7. Core Story 004 — Ershou Lake: From a Polluted Lake to a Cleaner Public Place Why this is now a core story This story has a clear before-and-after change, a real place, a family connection, a low-cost family outing, and a future-policy opinion. It is ready for EV02, OB09, and the main place routes. The central chain is: Ershou Lake near my hometown → dirty and unpleasant in the past → local government introduced environmental measures and developed the area → the lake became cleaner and more attractive → more people started visiting → I now walk there with my family → I would support stricter anti-littering and ecosystem-protection rules The confirmed local fact is that environmental cleanup or protection measures were introduced. Do not call those measures a named law. OB01 now uses a separate, officially verified plastic-shopping-bag regulation. 1. Background The lake is called Ershou Lake and is near my hometown. My grandparents used to go fishing there in the past. It was not a particularly famous place before. In the past, the lake was dirty and sometimes smelled unpleasant. Later, the local government introduced environmental cleanup or protection measures and developed the surrounding area for tourism. The area gradually became cleaner and more attractive to visitors. I now sometimes walk around the lake with my family. 2. The environmental change Before The lake looked less attractive. The water and surrounding environment were dirtier. There was an unpleasant smell. The area was not a major place for visitors. After Environmental cleanup and management improved the area. The lake became cleaner. Tourism and nearby commercial activity developed. More people began visiting the area. It became a more pleasant place for local families to walk and relax. A natural sentence: One thing I've noticed is that the whole area has changed a lot. It used to be quite dirty and unpleasant, but after the local government introduced environmental measures, it gradually became much cleaner and more attractive. 3. Independent Card — OB01: Paid Use of Plastic Shopping Bags Why this is an independent card This is a real national regulation selected for OB01 — A law or regulation about environmental protection. It is separate from the Ershou Lake story because the lake cleanup has no verified legal title. The central chain is: national regulation → effective from 1 June 2008 → supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets → plastic shopping bags must be sold rather than given away → clear price → encourage people to use fewer bags → conserve resources and protect the environment 1. Verified facts The official Chinese title is 《商品零售场所塑料购物袋有偿使用管理办法》. It was issued jointly by the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission, and the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce. It took effect on 1 June 2008. It applies to retail venues including supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets. These retailers must charge consumers for plastic shopping bags and clearly display the price. They may not provide the bags free of charge or disguise a free bag through another promotion. The stated purpose is to conserve resources, protect the environment, and encourage consumers to use fewer plastic shopping bags. A later national measure effective in 2023 still requires retail businesses to follow this paid-use regulation. 2. Speakable English blocks Introduce the regulation I'd like to talk about China's regulation on the paid use of plastic shopping bags. Explain the rule It took effect in 2008 and requires supermarkets, shopping malls, and open markets to charge customers for plastic shopping bags instead of giving them away for free. Explain the purpose Its main purpose is to reduce unnecessary use of plastic bags, conserve resources, and protect the environment. Explain why the design makes sense The rule does not completely ban plastic bags. Instead, it makes their cost visible, which can encourage shoppers to bring reusable bags or think twice before taking a new one. 3. Useful vocabulary paid use of plastic shopping bags charge customers for a bag provide something free of charge display the price clearly retail venue supermarket / shopping mall / open market reusable shopping bag reduce unnecessary consumption conserve resources plastic pollution environmental regulation 4. One-minute preparation keywords China → 2008 → paid plastic bags → supermarkets / malls / markets → no free bags → clear price → fewer unnecessary bags → reusable bags → resources + environment 5. Factual boundaries Call it a regulation or administrative measure, not necessarily a law passed by the legislature. Do not say China completely banned all plastic bags. The paid-use rule concerns plastic shopping bags supplied by retail venues. It excludes certain plastic pre-packaging bags used for hygiene and food-safety purposes, such as bags for loose fresh or cooked food. Do not connect this national regulation to the cleanup of Ershou Lake. 6. Core Story 005 — My Sister's Education Decisions Why this is a core story This card contains two real decisions involving the same family member. Use the university-choice event for giving advice and the later postgraduate-study decision for feeling proud of a family member. Do not merge the two timelines into one event. The EV17 chain is: sister finishes an important exam → grades limit the available choices → she also has preferences about majors → my mother and I research universities with her → compare universities and majors → narrow down the options → help her make a final choice → feel relieved The separate EV18 chain is: sister has a stable job → decides to leave it → pursues the postgraduate degree she genuinely wants → accepts uncertainty instead of staying only for security → I admire her courage and feel proud of her Do not memorize a full answer. Memorize the decision-making process. 1. Background This happened several years ago when my sister needed to choose a university. Her exam results were an important factor because they affected which universities she could realistically apply to. She also had her own preferences about what subject or major she wanted to study. My mother and I helped her research the available choices. 2. What we actually did We searched online for universities that matched her grades. We looked at the majors available at different universities. We compared several options instead of choosing the first one we found. We considered both practical limits and her own interests. We discussed the advantages and disadvantages together. Finally, we helped her narrow the list down and make a decision. A natural sentence: My mother and I helped my sister research different universities and compare the majors they offered, based on both her grades and what she was interested in. 3. Why this was real collaboration This was not only one person giving help. My sister had to explain what she wanted. My mother and I helped collect and compare information. We discussed the options together. The final choice was made through a shared decision-making process. This makes the story useful for a working-with-a-family-member question if that question appears in another speaking bank. Possible line: We worked on it together because each of us contributed something different: my sister knew what she wanted, while my mother and I helped her compare the realistic options. 4. Strong route — EV17: A time when you gave advice to others Best spotlight Focus on: sister needs to choose university → many options → research → compare majors and universities → give advice → final decision What the advice was The advice was not simply: “Choose this university.” It was more like: choose an option that matches both your academic results and your genuine interest in the subject. Possible line: I tried not to make the decision for her. Instead, I helped her compare the choices and encouraged her to think about both the university and the major. 5. Strong route — EV18: A time when you felt proud of a family member This is a separate, later decision from the university-choice event above. My sister had a stable job. She chose to give it up so that she could pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted. The decision meant leaving security behind and accepting uncertainty. I felt proud of her because she had the courage to choose the path she truly valued. Natural IELTS wording: I felt proud of my sister when she gave up a stable job to pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted. I admired her courage because she was willing to leave a secure path and accept uncertainty for something that mattered to her. Factual boundary: Do not claim that she completed the degree, entered a named programme, or achieved a particular result unless those facts are confirmed later. Do not present this as the result of the earlier university-choice discussion. 6. Family-help route This story can also support questions about helping a family member. Focus on: important decision → she needed information → we researched together → I explained or compared options → she became more confident about the choice Possible line: I wanted to help because choosing a university can affect several years of someone's life, so I felt it was worth spending time on the decision. 7. Useful vocabulary university application academic results grades major / field of study available options compare different universities narrow down the choices weigh the pros and cons make an informed decision give advice respect someone's preference realistic option make the final choice work through a decision together leave a stable job pursue a postgraduate degree give up a secure path accept uncertainty have the courage to follow what she genuinely wants 8. Useful phrases from the phrase bank Explain comparison We looked at several options before making a decision. Explain balanced advice We tried to balance what was realistic with what she genuinely wanted. Explain collaboration We worked through the decision together. Explain pride I was proud of her because she had the courage to leave a stable job and pursue the postgraduate degree she genuinely wanted. 9. Core Story 006 — Renhe Xincheng: A Convenient but Boring Shopping Center Why this is a core story This is a real place near my home that can naturally cover three topics: PL05 — A boring place PL07 — A tall building in your city you like or dislike PL08 — A shopping mall The central idea is not that the shopping center has nothing in it. In fact, it has many normal facilities. The reason I find it boring is that the experience feels repetitive and not very innovative. The central chain is: shopping center near my home → clothes / coffee / food / cinema / promotions → I sometimes go with friends or family → every visit feels similar → nothing feels unique → convenient but boring 1. Basic background The shopping center is called Renhe Xincheng. It is near my home. It is a tall commercial building. Its exterior looks like an ordinary high-rise and has not left a distinctive visual impression on me. It has common facilities such as: clothing shops coffee shops restaurants or food options a cinema It sometimes has promotional activities or small events. 2. What I usually do there With friends I mainly go there to watch movies. The cinema is probably the main reason I visit with friends. With family I sometimes go there with my parents. We may have coffee or spend a little time there. A natural sentence: I don't go there because I love shopping. Most of the time, I only go there to watch a movie with friends or have a coffee with my parents. 3. Why I find it boring The problem is not that there are no activities. The real problem is: the shops are very similar to those in many other malls the promotions feel repetitive there is not much that feels new or surprising most of the activities are things I could do in almost any shopping center after a short time, I feel there is nothing else I really want to explore A strong natural explanation: Even though there are quite a few things to do, I still find it boring because every visit feels almost the same. The shops, promotions, and activities are quite predictable, so there is rarely anything that makes me curious or excited. 4. Core Story 007 — My Smartphone: Expensive but Essential Why this is a core story This is one real object that supports two cue cards: OB10 — An item on which you spent more than expected: content-ready. OB15 — Something you cannot live without: content-ready. The facts stay mostly the same. Only the spotlight changes: OB10: focus on the purchase, budget, and why the final cost was higher than expected. OB15: focus on how often you use the phone and why it has become essential in daily life. The central chain is: previous 256 GB experience required deleting apps → planned to buy another 256 GB smartphone → changed to the 512 GB version at the time of purchase → paid about 2,000 yuan more → no longer worry about storage → worth the extra cost → use it every day 1. Basic background The object is my smartphone. My previous 256 GB phone often ran short of storage, so I regularly deleted apps that I did not use very often. I originally planned to buy the 256 GB version. At the time of purchase, I suddenly decided to buy the 512 GB version instead. The storage upgrade made the final cost higher than I had expected. After upgrading, I no longer needed to worry about storage space, so I felt the extra cost was worthwhile. Even so, I use it every day and depend on it for many practical tasks. 2. Strong route — OB10: An item on which you spent more than expected Status: content-ready. Best spotlight Focus on: previous 256 GB storage problem → planned 256 GB version → changed my mind at purchase → chose 512 GB → paid about 2,000 yuan more → no storage anxiety → worthwhile Confirmed reason the cost was higher I originally planned to buy the 256 GB version, but I changed my mind at the time of purchase and chose the 512 GB version instead. That sudden storage upgrade made the phone cost more than I had expected. The approximate difference was 2,000 yuan. With 512 GB, I no longer had to keep deleting less frequently used apps. I felt the extra cost was worthwhile because it solved a problem I had experienced repeatedly. Do not add better performance, camera quality, accessories, or longer service life as reasons unless they are separately confirmed. Natural closing line: Although I spent about 2,000 yuan more than I had planned, I think it was worth it because I no longer have to worry about running out of storage or constantly delete apps. 3. Core Story 008 — Boston: From a NeRF Project at MIT to a Celtics Game Why this is a core story This Boston experience now has three concrete scenes and one clear reflection: short summer project at MIT → use NeRF to reconstruct 3D models from video → get up early for the final poster presentation → place second among groups with the same topic → watch the Celtics at TD Garden → revise my view of Boston → reflect on teamwork and balancing research with everyday life It can answer the early-morning and live-sports questions without inventing a second trip. Boston is confirmed as my genuine favourite visited city. The NeRF branch may support a future technology or project question only after the exact smoothing method and result are confirmed. 1. Background I went to Boston for a short summer project at MIT. The project involved using NeRF technology to turn video footage into three-dimensional models. The reconstruction process produced visible noise or artifacts in the 3D models. My responsibility was to smooth the reconstructed models and reduce those artifacts. On the final day, our team presented the project with a poster and placed second among the groups working on the same topic. During the same stay, I watched an NBA game at TD Garden. A concise non-technical explanation of the project: It was a short computer-vision project in which we used NeRF to reconstruct three-dimensional models from video footage. 2. The NeRF project scene Goal Use video footage as the input. Apply NeRF-related techniques to reconstruct a 3D model or scene. Problem The reconstructed models contained noise and visual artifacts. These artifacts made the surfaces look less clean or realistic. My responsibility I was responsible for smoothing the reconstructed models. The purpose was to reduce the visible noise and improve the quality of the final 3D result. Natural IELTS wording: My main responsibility was dealing with the noise in the reconstructed models. I worked on smoothing the surfaces and reducing visual artifacts so that the final result would look cleaner. Do not name a specific smoothing algorithm until it is confirmed. 3. Getting up early for the final presentation On the final day of the project, I needed to get up at 7:00 a.m.. I normally got up at about 9:00 a.m., so this was early by my usual standard. Our team needed extra time to coordinate the presentation. We confirmed the division of speaking responsibilities and prepared the project poster. The presentation was completed successfully. Our team placed second among the groups working on the same project topic. I felt that all our work had been worthwhile and felt grateful to my teammates. A concise version: On the final day, I got up at seven instead of my usual nine because our team needed to coordinate the presentation and prepare our poster. We eventually placed second among the groups working on the same topic, so I felt that the early start and all our effort had been worthwhile. 4. The Celtics game at TD Garden I watched an NBA game in person at TD Garden. The Boston Celtics played another NBA team, but I no longer remember the opponent. The opponent's name is not necessary for the story and should not be guessed. What impressed me most was the patience and support of the home crowd. When the Celtics were attacking, the audience shouted words such as “Go, Celtics, go!” When the team was defending, the crowd repeatedly shouted “Defense!” and created a very loud atmosphere. The strongest scene: The most memorable part was not the final score. It was hearing the whole crowd change its chant with the game: they cheered for the Celtics on offense and shouted “Defense!” when the other team had the ball. 5. Change in my view of Boston Before I mainly associated Boston with universities, researchers, and a serious academic atmosphere. After the experience The Celtics game showed me a much more energetic and community-oriented side of the city. I began to see Boston as a place where academic life and ordinary leisure can exist together. The contrast between the MIT project and TD Garden made the city especially memorable. Personal reflection This is a personal conclusion, not a universal claim about every researcher: The experience made me realize that research does not have to occupy every part of a person's life. Having interests outside work may help people protect their mental health, remain creative, and return to research with new energy. 6. Core Story 009 - Jensen Huang and My Long-term AI Ambition Why this is a core story This material connects one public figure with one genuine personal ambition: choosing a GPU for my first computer -> learning about Jensen Huang and NVIDIA -> respecting his long-term judgment on GPU computing, CUDA, and AI -> wanting to ask how he recognized that opportunity -> connecting the question to my own ambition to build a more advanced AI assistant It can support four cue cards, but the spotlight must change for each one. It is not necessary to explain the technical project in detail during the exam. 1. How I learned about Jensen Huang I first became aware of NVIDIA when I needed to choose a GPU for my first personal computer. I later learned more about Jensen Huang through technology news and NVIDIA product launches or keynote presentations. I do not follow businesspeople closely, so this should not be presented as a lifelong admiration story. A concise version: I first learned about Jensen Huang when I was choosing a GPU for my first computer, and I later saw more about him through technology news and NVIDIA keynote presentations. 2. Why I respect him and want to meet him He is a co-founder of NVIDIA and a well-known technology business leader. What I respect most is his long-term judgment and commitment to GPU computing, CUDA, and AI computing before their full commercial value became obvious. I would like to ask how he recognized the long-term potential of accelerated computing and maintained that strategy over time. This question matters to me because I also want to work in artificial intelligence and make sound long-term technical choices. The central idea is foresight and long-term judgment, not company valuation alone. A concise version: What I respect most is his long-term judgment. I would like to ask how he recognized the potential of GPU and AI computing before the opportunity became obvious to everyone. 3. My long-term ambition My long-term goal is to create an intelligent AI assistant with a persistent internal affective state. This state should influence the system's memory, judgment, and actions over time. The early inspiration came from watching Iron Man as a child and seeing JARVIS as more than a simple command-following tool. The idea became a serious long-term ambition around the beginning of university, approximately three years ago. What interests me most about AI is that models trained through prediction can display surprisingly complex abilities. This also gives us an engineering route for investigating how intelligence may arise. A concise exam version: My long-term ambition is to build an AI assistant with a persistent internal affective state that can influence its memory, judgment, and actions, rather than one that only responds to individual commands. 4. Actions I have already taken I have studied artificial intelligence and model training. I have learned about agent architecture design. I have started a related GitHub project. The project is ongoing and unfinished. This is enough detail for Part 2: I have studied model training and agent design, and I have also started a small ongoing GitHub project related to this idea. The project name, architecture, and implementation details are not required unless a later cue card explicitly asks about a project. 5. Single-topic Card PL03 - A Friend's Apartment I Enjoyed Visiting but Would Not Live In Status This is a verified personal material card for PL03. I enjoyed visiting my friend and playing games with him, but I would not want to live in his family's apartment. 1. Why I visited My friend and I arranged to spend time together. I went to his apartment to play video games with him. We played games such as NBA 2K and FIFA. The visit was enjoyable because I liked spending time and gaming with my friend. A concise description: I once visited a friend's apartment because we had arranged to spend the day playing video games such as NBA 2K and FIFA. I enjoyed the visit because we had a good time together. 2. Who else was there My friend lived with his parents and younger brother. His parents and brother were at home during my visit. I did not know them well. I did not always know what to say to them and worried that my presence might disturb the family. A concise version: His parents and younger brother were also at home. Because I did not know them well, I sometimes felt awkward and worried that I might be disturbing their family time. 3. What the apartment was like The apartment looked untidy. His younger brother's toys were scattered across the desk and the floor. This made the space feel cluttered rather than comfortable for me. A concise scene: The apartment was also quite untidy, with his younger brother's toys scattered across both the desk and the floor. 4. Why I would not want to live there I would feel uncomfortable living with relatives whom I did not know well. I would constantly worry about disturbing the family. The clutter would also make it difficult for me to relax. These concerns do not mean that I disliked my friend or regretted the visit. A balanced reflection: I was happy to visit and play games with my friend, but living there would be different. I would probably feel awkward around family members I did not know well, and the cluttered environment would make it harder for me to relax. 5. Cue-card route PL03 - A friend's home you visited but do not want to live in Focus on: friend's apartment -> arranged to play games -> NBA 2K + FIFA -> parents and younger brother present -> not close to them -> awkward/no conversation -> worry about disturbing them -> toys on desk and floor -> enjoyable visit -> unsuitable for living 6. Useful vocabulary visit a friend's apartment arrange to spend time together play video games his parents and younger brother not know someone well not know what to talk about feel awkward around someone worry about disturbing the family an untidy apartment toys scattered across the floor a cluttered environment enjoy visiting but not want to live there 7. One-minute preparation keywords friend's apartment -> gaming visit -> NBA 2K/FIFA -> parents + brother -> unfamiliar -> awkward -> disturb family -> toys everywhere -> clutter -> enjoyed visit -> would not live there 8. Factual boundaries I visited to play games; I did not stay overnight. Do not invent the apartment's location, size, number of rooms, or decoration. Do not claim that the family treated me badly. The discomfort came from unfamiliarity, concern about disturbing them, and clutter. I enjoyed spending time with my friend despite not wanting to live in the apartment. Single-topic Card PL09 - My Bed as My Favourite Place to Relax at Home Status This is a verified personal material card for PL09. My favourite place to relax at home is my bed. 1. What I do there I lie on the bed and use my phone. I play games. I watch or scroll through short videos. These are simple leisure activities rather than work or study tasks. A concise description: My favourite place to relax at home is my bed. I usually lie there, use my phone, play games, or scroll through short videos. 2. When I use it I often relax there on weekend mornings. I also spend time there before going to sleep at night. These are the two clearest time windows for this routine. A concise version: I normally spend time there on weekend mornings or at night before I go to sleep. 3. Why it is comfortable I can lie down instead of sitting upright. Lying down feels less tiring than sitting. The bed is soft and physically comfortable. The lighting around the bed is softer than in other parts of the home. The softer light contributes to a calmer atmosphere. A concise explanation: I prefer the bed because lying down feels much easier than sitting, and the soft surface is more comfortable. The lighting there is also gentler than in other parts of my home, which creates a calmer atmosphere. 4. How it affects me Spending time there reduces my stress. Relaxing there before bed makes it easier for me to fall asleep. A concise reflection: After relaxing there for a while, I usually feel less stressed, and at night it also becomes easier for me to fall asleep. 5. Cue-card route PL09 - Your favourite place in your home where you can relax Focus on: my bed -> weekend mornings + before sleep -> lie down -> phone/games/short videos -> softer than sitting -> comfortable bed -> gentle lighting -> calmer atmosphere -> less stress -> easier sleep 6. Useful vocabulary my favourite place to unwind lie on my bed scroll through short videos play games on my phone on weekend mornings before going to sleep sit upright a soft and comfortable surface gentle lighting create a calm atmosphere reduce my stress fall asleep more easily 7. One-minute preparation keywords bed -> weekend morning/night -> lie down -> phone -> games/videos -> softer than sitting -> gentle light -> calm -> less stress -> easier sleep 8. Factual boundaries Do not invent the room's size, colour scheme, furniture, view, or decoration. Do not add reading, music, studying, or conversations unless later confirmed. No exact duration for the routine has been confirmed. The softer lighting is a real comparison with other parts of the home. The main effects are reduced stress and easier sleep. Verified Micro-materials from the Conversation Review These materials are real but currently too small for a full Core Story. Keep them as compact fact cards rather than padding them with invented events. Micro-material A — Walking after dinner Confirmed facts I usually take a walk around my home after dinner. I associate the habit with digestion, relaxation, and better sleep. The walk also gives me time to review what happened during the day and clear my mind. Potential uses a healthy habit an activity that helps me relax something I do after a busy day a simple way to improve well-being Details still needed for a full story the usual route and duration; whether I walk alone or with someone; one specific occasion or noticeable change caused by the habit. Micro-material B — Spicy food from my hometown Confirmed facts My hometown is known for spicy food. When I return, I like trying local specialties. Examples mentioned in the conversation include spicy hotpot and spicy fish. Potential uses food from my hometown a local specialty I would recommend something I like doing when I return home local culture or a hometown description Factual boundary This material does not currently cover OB07, food eaten during a special event. Returning home and eating local food is not automatically a special event. Details still needed for a full story the hometown's name, if I want to use it; one specific restaurant, family meal, or visit; which dish I prefer and why; one sensory detail and my genuine reaction. Blank Core Story Template Core Story ___ — [Story title] Primary cue card [Paste the cue card here.] Core idea [One or two sentences.] Background Cause or motivation What I did Memorable scene [Describe one real moment.] Results Feelings and reflection Useful vocabulary Useful phrases Reusable cue cards One-minute preparation keywords keyword → keyword → keyword → keyword → result → lesson
